A former far-right activist, who has a string of convictions including for harassing a Jewish MP, has stood down as a Conservative candidate in upcoming local elections after major backlash.

Withdrawing from the race, Joshua Bonehill-Paine said he acknowledged that “my previous actions continue to cause pain in the Jewish community”.

But he hit out at other political parties, saying that if he did stand they would “spend all their time focusing on my past rather than the work I'm doing today, or even fighting antisemitism in their own midst”.

open image in gallery Joshua Bonehill-Paine was jailed for racially aggravated harassment against Labour peer Luciana Berger (Met Police/PA) ( Metropolitan Police )

He revealed that Tory leader Kemi Badenoch, who had previously defended his selection, has offered him a role as an adviser on how to tackle the radicalisation of young men.

“Rather than standing as a local council candidate, I believe that my experience is better used supporting Kemi Badenoch in her ongoing mission to combat the antisemitism and extremism that is dividing our nation,” Mr Bonehill-Paine said in a statement on X, formerly Twitter.

“I have therefore informed the party of my decision to withdraw from next year’s council election and Kemi has instead offered that I become an adviser to the Conservative Party’s Culture and Integration Commission, specifically focusing on how young men become radicalised.”

In response, Ms Badenoch said she was “sad” about his decision but “glad he is going to work with me and the party”.

But Reform UK said it “beggars belief” that he had been appointed as an adviser.

Earlier, Mr Bonehill-Paine said he was “tremendously proud” to have been selected to stand as a candidate for Crewkerne South in next year’s Somerset Council elections.

open image in gallery Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch defended his selection ( Reuters )

Mr Bonehill-Paine, who now runs a political satire account on social media posting AI videos, is a former neo-Nazi activist who has several convictions, including posting anti-Semitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally.

In 2016 he was found guilty of harassing former MP Luciana Berger in a string of anti-Jewish rants, posting articles online calling her a "dominatrix" and "an evil money-grabber" with a "deep-rooted hatred of men".

He was previously jailed for producing an advert for a neo-Nazi rally illustrated with a picture of Nazi concentration camp Auschwitz which promised “an absolute gas”.

Since then he has apologised for his past offending, and said he was now dedicated to “challenging the wave of hatred British Jews continue to face”.

Hours before he stood down, Jewish leaders rejected Ms Badenoch’s offer of a meeting with him, as she defended his selection as a council candidate.

In a joint statement, the Board of Deputies and the JLC said they had declined an invitation to meet Mr Bonehill-Paine, describing him as “a former neo-Nazi with criminal convictions for antisemitic hatred”.

open image in gallery Mr Bonehill-Paine was jailed in 2016 over antisemitic abuse of Lady Berger (Jonathan Brady/PA) ( PA )

They said: “The severity of Joshua Bonehill-Paine’s crimes targeting Luciana Berger and others mean that he still faces ongoing legal restrictions.

“Whilst we do believe in the possibility of rehabilitation, this should not in this case entail selection as a candidate for a major political party, and the impact of this decision on the victims ought to be a central consideration.”

Ms Badenoch defended his selection on Wednesday, saying she believed he had been rehabilitated.

She told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “I am extremely worried about antisemitism and what I feel is that if we can’t have the people who have previously been radicalised, who understand what went wrong and are part of the fight against antisemitism now. If we’re saying: ‘No, no, no, you’re untouchable,’ then how can we pretend that we believe in rehabilitation?”

But she suggested she would not allow him to stand for Parliament, and that as a councillor he would mainly be in charge of issues such as bins.

She said: “I’m not giving him a national platform, he is standing to be a councillor in Somerset… it is a local platform looking at parking, sorting out bins. I have much higher thresholds for what it takes to be a Conservative MP.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

Sports.title: Luis Figo has brutally taken down Gianni Infantino - now he should succeed him
Sports.content:
Luis Figo has brutally taken down Gianni Infantino - now he should succeed him

The Portuguese legend has pulled no punches in laying into the FIFA president eleven years after briefly putting himself forward for the same role

View 3 Images Luis Figo has called on Gianni Infantino to resign immediately

It is now getting to the stage where some people of a significantly forgiving nature might actually begin to feel a little bit sorry for Gianni Infantino. Of course, he brought it all on himself - not just with his heinous scheme to sell off the World Cup but with his entire power-obsessed, egotistical tenure as FIFA president.

‌



But the tirade of criticism has been something else. And one of the most cutting character assessments has now come from the breed of ‘legend’ that Infantino has tried to ingratiate himself with over the past decade.

‌



Luis Figo referred to Infantino’s conduct as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour” he has ever witnessed. “And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game,” Figo said, before going on to describe Infantino as “a relic of the game’s past.”

‌



Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Figo then proceeds to accuse Infantino of inflicting “a litany of abuses … on football’s reputation” during a “reign of terrible self-interest.” And the Portuguese legend was just warming up.

“Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate,” said the former Barcelona and Real Madrid player. “He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest of the game he is supposed to serve.

“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

‌



Brutal stuff. Almost certainly nothing that most right-minded football followers would disagree with, but brutal all the same.

Figo is right, of course. Infantino has to go. But what Figo - a close confidante of UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin - does not suggest, it seems, is that someone such as himself should now step forward.

View 3 Images Arsene Wenger has denouned Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheme but not the man himself (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



For a couple of months in early 2015, Figo did just that. Backed by figures such as David Beckham and Jose Mourinho no less, Figo launched his candidacy for the FIFA presidency at Wembley in February 2015.

I remember his manifesto brochure. Expanding the World Cup to 48 teams was one of his key policies, by the way. Figo was standing against Sepp Blatter - who would go on to win a fifth term - but pulled out shortly before the May election.

Which was a shame. Figo might have made a good president. And what is to stop him running against Infantino? Or more likely, what is to stop him running in a contest to succeed Infantino, who will surely not run for re-election?

‌



The main theme of the backlash to the Infantino proposal that will now go down as one of the most infamous in the game’s history has been that football belongs to the people, belongs to the fans. Well, what sort of character would the fans want as the figurehead of the world’s governing body?

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is now under immense pressure to step aside from the FIFA presidency

They would not have wanted a Swiss lawyer in the first place, that is for sure. Ironically, they might have wanted someone like Arsene Wenger.

‌



After a few days’ silence, FIFA’s chief of global football development denounced Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise Scheme but did not individually denounce the man who gave him his lucrative gig. Wenger might be too allied to Infantino, and has himself had the odd madcap idea recently.

But perhaps he should stand against Infantino or stand to succeed him. Wenger has always claimed to have the good of the game at heart.

That is unlikely to happen but the more options we have from those who know about the game rather than the politics of the game, the better. And it would be good if those options included Figo.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Danny Welbeck and five players get 5s as Blues beaten by Juventus
Sports.content:
Chelsea suffered the second defeat of their pre-season tour as Serie A side Juventus ran out 1-0 winners at the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong. A second-half strike from Edon Zhegrova was enough for the Serie A side in a game that lacked any real quality - aside from the finish for the goal.

The Blues dominated possession, but Juventus had the better of the opportunities. The Italian side forced Robert Sanchez into a number of decent first-half saves before eventually finding the breakthrough in the second half.

Zhegrova curled in a brilliant effort from outside the box into the top corner, leaving substitute goalkeeper Mike Penders with no chance of saving it. Alonso's side beat Western Sydney Wanderers 6-4 before a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur last week.

It's now back-to-back defeats for the Blues, with Mykhailo Mudryk making his long-awaited return during the match. Here are the player ratings from Hong Kong...

‌



Chelsea sanctions reveal same punishment for sexual misconduct and ticket transferring READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea player ratings

Robert Sanchez - 7

Pulled off some good saves, keeping out Jeremie Boga on two occasions. He was the busier of the two goalkeepers, but wasn't really threatened.

Marco Palestra - 7

‌



Linked up well with Quenda down the right-hand side and defended well on the whole.

Wesley Fofana - 6

Didn't really put a foot wrong in the first half. Defended well and limited Arkadiusz Milik to very little.

Tosin Adarabioyo - 6

‌



Like his defensive partner, he kept Milik very quiet and looked assured on the ball at the back.

Jorrel Hato - 6

Defended well on the whole, but Juventus started to get some joy down his side as the first half wore on.

Geovany Quenda - 7

‌



Looked a threat down the right, put some dangerous balls into the box. A bright showing.

Moises Caicedo - 8

Chelsea's best outfield player. Dictated the play when the Blues had possession and had the most touches on the ball.

View 3 Images Moises Caicedo was impressive for Chelsea against Juventus. (Image: (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images))

‌



Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli - 6

Has impressed so far in pre-season and didn't look out of place playing alongside some world-class players.

Jamie Gittens - 7

Enjoyed some nice runs down the left flank, but lacked an end product.

‌



Danny Welbeck - 5

His first minutes for Chelsea since his move to the club, he worked hard but had little to show for it, bar one close effort.

Jaoa Pedro - 5

Less involved than his fellow forward, a quiet outing compared to his usual standards.

‌



Substitutes

Nicolas Jackson - 4 (45 - on for Welbeck)

Came on for Welbeck and gave Chelsea a bit more mobility up front, but again, offered little if anything.

Mamadou Sarr - 6 (45 on for Tosin)

Steady if not spectacular.

‌



Estevao - 7 (45 on for Quenda)

Caused havoc down the right after coming on at the half-time interval. Juventus really struggled to deal with him.

Mike Penders - 6 (45 on for Sanchez)

An imposing presence for Chelsea in between the sticks. Commanded his area well, and there was nothing he could do with the Juve goal.

‌



Dario Essugo - 5 (65 for Caicedo)

Took the captain's armband when he came onto the pitch and struggled. Wanted too much time on the ball.

Liam Delap - 5 (65 for Pedro)

Didn't get into the game after coming on in place of Pedro, went on a few decent runs, but no end product.

‌



View 3 Images Mykhailo Mudryk made his first appearance for Chelsea in 20 months

Romeo Lavia - 6 (65 for Nicoll-Jazuli)

Worked hard after coming off the bench, but didn't really impact the game.

Aaron Anselmino - 5 (65 for Hato)

‌



The goal came down his side and needed to be closer to Zhegrova for the Juventus opener

Josh Acheampong - 6 (65 for Palestra)

Offered less than Palestra going forward, but was solid defensively.

Olutayo Subuloye - 5 (65 for Fofana)

‌



Needed to get out to Zhegrova quicker and close him down for the Juventus opener.

Dastan Satpaev - 6 (65 for Gittens)

Bright when he came on. Tried to make things happen and wasn't afraid to demand the ball.

Mykhailo Mudryk - 6 (80 for Jackson)

‌



Barely touched the ball after coming on for a 10-minute cameo, his first football for Chelsea in 20 months.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr final transfer decision imminent as Arsenal players 'think deal is done'
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr final transfer decision imminent as Arsenal players 'think deal is done'

Vinicius Jr to Arsenal is gathering serious momentum with the stance of Mikel Arteta's squad suggesting that a sensational move for the Real Madrid star is firmly on the cards

View 2 Images Arsenal's players think a deal for Vinicius Jr is at an advanced stage (Image: (Photo by Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images))

The Arsenal squad are of the belief that Vinicius Jr joining from Real Madrid is a 'done deal', according to reports in Spain.

‌



The Brazil international is of concrete interest to those at Emirates Stadium with decisive talks over his future in the Spanish capital taking place. A meeting between his agents and the club reportedly took place on Wednesday which suggests a final decision on his future is set to be made.

‌



As he only has 12 months left on his current deal, confidence is growing at Arsenal over what would be a sensational transfer. Sporting director Andrea Berta is working on the deal with the players already accepting it as more than likely he joins, according to AS, having also been convinced of a move to the Gunners by Mikel Arteta.

‌



How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

Their report states that the Arsenal boss has already spoken with Vinicius to explain what his role would be. Such conversations have filtered into the dressing room with Berta reportedly stating to players that the club are trying to secure what would likely be the most expensive Premier League signing ever.

The funds for such a seismic deal are seemingly available, however, with it specifically stated that there is a strong desire, perhaps more so than in Madrid, within Arsenal to finalise an agreement. There is a gap of €8million (£6.4m) per-year between what Real are willing to offer and what Vinicius wants in order to extend, even after reports of a fresh proposal being made.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Vinicius re-joined training with Los Blancos earlier this week following his mandatory three-week break after the World Cup with the plan for Wednesday being that he would train at 10am before a meeting with his agents and Real took place at 11am.

View 2 Images Arsenal have already finalised a deal for Vinicius Jr's fellow Brazilian Bruno Guimaraes

Exactly what was discussed or even agreed upon is unknown but the most recent updates certainly suggest it could be good news for Arsenal.

‌



While Arsenal players may believe the Vinicius Jr deal is done, Bruno Guimaraes' switch to the Premier League champions from Newcastle United has been finalised.

The 28-year-old is set to cost £75m and thus take Arsenal's spending into the triple-figures following Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapie joining permanently. Illan Meslier was also signed as a free agent.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford primed for Ruben Amorim reunion after Man Utd transfer twist

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after his Barcelona loan ended and the forward could play against former boss Ruben Amorim later this month

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford and Ruben Amorim's issues at Man Utd were well documented (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford could be poised to make his long awaited Manchester United return against AC Milan - now managed by Ruben Amorim.

‌



The forward has not played for the Red Devils since the Portuguese boss was in charge. It was under Amorim that Rashford's struggles began as the pair clashed, which saw him twice head out on loan.

‌



Initially he moved to Aston Villa for the second half of the 24/25 campaign and then secured a switch to Barcelona, where he spent last season. The Spanish side opted against signing him permanently and Rashford has returned to Old Trafford with ambitions of becoming a regular again.

‌



If his return to United is in line with the club's other World Cup players, who have been afforded an extended break, then he is likely to be involved in next week's training camp in the Republic of Ireland. If so Rashford could find himself coming up against Amorim's Milan side with a friendly scheduled to take place on August 15.

Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical READ MORE :

There is a chance that Rashford could appear against Leeds at Croke Park on 12 August, but if so that would come with just a couple of days training behind him.

Amorim was axed by the Old Trafford bosses in January and, at his unveiling at Milan, apologised for his dire time in charge of the club. His style never took off at United and within weeks of being appointed it became obvious that he and Rashford had an issue as he continued to snub the forward.

‌



When he eventually opened up on their divide he confessed: "I couldn't get Marcus to see the way you're supposed to play football and to train the way I see it. Sometimes you have one player that is really good with one coach, and the same player with another coach is different."

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is due back for Man Utd pre-season once his post-World Cup break is over (Image: Getty)

The 28-year-old returns to Manchester off the back of a season that saw him score 11 times and come up with 14 assists as Barcelona won the La Liga title, the Spanish Super Cup and reached the last eight of the Champions League. Rashford still has a contract until 2028 and his weekly salary of £325,000 makes him the club's top earner.

‌



Rashford's biggest challenge will be forcing his way back into an attacking line that had £200million worth of talent added to it last summer. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko all came in and were pivotal in the team's upturn in form, leading them to finish third.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today

A crisis meeting has been called as pressure continues to mount on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA president is under serious threat (Image: Getty)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has summoned his top chiefs to a crunch crisis meeting today as he fights to save his job following the explosive fallout from his botched private equity deal. The embattled FIFA boss has called an emergency summit with senior leadership in Morocco in a desperate bid to shore up his position.

‌



It comes after he secretly hatched a highly controversial scheme to spin off the governing body's commercial operations into a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise.

‌



The project aimed to sell a 20 per cent stake in the commercial and tournament rights of the World Cup to private investors. Although a fierce global backlash and threats of a massive boycott from UEFA forced Infantino into a humiliating climbdown to scrap the proposal last week, furious football leaders insist the damage is done.

‌



While Infantino uses today's crisis talks in Rabat to try and stabilise his reign and cling to power, an outraged European football establishment is at open war with him and exploring two distinct legal avenues to force him out.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

The first option being discussed is triggering an emergency vote of no confidence. Under official FIFA statutes, an extraordinary Congress can be called if requested by at least 20 per cent of member associations - equating to 43 of FIFA's 211 global members.

‌



View 2 Images Infantino has called a crisis meeting as he scrambles to save his job (Image: Getty Images)

With UEFA alone boasting 55 member associations, European football easily clears that threshold on its own to force a congress within three months.

However, actually ousting Infantino at the meeting would still require a simple majority of all 211 global members, where every nation holds a single vote regardless of size.

‌



The second option - and a far more explosive route to remove Infantino - is through formal disciplinary action. FIFA's independent Ethics Committee has the authority to investigate alleged breaches of the FIFA Code of Ethics and hand down severe sanctions, including lengthy bans from all football-related activities.

This is the exact mechanism that brought down former president Sepp Blatter in 2015. Whilst no official ethics investigation has been opened yet, a lengthy ban remains the ultimate nuclear option to force him out immediately.

If Infantino is ousted before his term ends, FIFA's Governance Regulations state the longest-serving vice president would take temporary charge until Congress elects a replacement.

The next official presidential election is scheduled for March 18, 2027, with nominations closing on November 18. Infantino had previously been expected to win by a landslide but after pushing the game to the brink, he may find today's crisis summit marks the beginning of the end.

Sports.title: Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical
Sports.content:
Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical

Manchester United are ready to sanction the exits of two goalkeepers in Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek having signed two this summer to back up Senne Lammens

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir is set for a move to La Liga

Manchester United continue to overhaul their goalkeeping ranks with Altay Bayindir set to depart for Spain and Radek Vitek on the verge of a move to the Championship.

‌



The situation between the sticks at Old Trafford has kept changing over the past three years with Senne Lammens establishing himself as the club's new No 1 last term. Underneath him players have left in search of more minutes, which has ultimately led Bayindir to head overseas.

‌



The Turkish goalkeeper spent the majority of his time at Old Trafford as a back-up, starting just six times in the Premier League last term, and a deal has now been agreed with Celta Vigo.

‌



He will join on a season-long loan with his wages covered by the La Liga side. Celta Vigo have the option to make the move permanent for £3.5million and it is understood United have a high sell-on clause attached in the deal.

Vitek, the 22-year-old Czech who impressed last season at Bristol City, is on his way back to the second tier as he prepares to join Middlesbrough, subject to a medical, in deal worth up to £14m. United retain a buy back option as well as a sell on clause that, Sky Sports claim, is a hefty 35 percent.

To cover for those departures United have signed Karl Darlow from Leeds after he became available on a free. He played 24 times for the Whites last term as they retained Premier League status. United also bought in teenage goalkeeper Kit Margetson from Swansea at the end of July.

‌



The moves continue to see United's goalkeeping landscape change. Lammens came in this time last year as an unknown quantity from Royal Antwerp but within months of arriving was promoted to become the team's first choice, keeping eight clean sheets as United finished third.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is closing in on a move to Middlesbrough

His rise came after Andre Onana's surprise departure. The Cameroonian had endured a difficult time in Manchester having arrived from Inter Milan with an impressive reputation, but he continued to make notable errors that cost the team. He was allowed to leave on loan for Trabzonspor, who paid his wages in full.

‌



He has since returned to the Super Lig outfit for another year. Onana was ultimately signed by Erik ten Hag to replace David de Gea, who was allowed to leave on a free after spending more than a decade as the team's undisputed No 1.

Sports.title: Celtic boss O'Neill in hospital after undergoing 'small procedure'
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill remains in hospital after undergoing "a small procedure", Celtic have confirmed.

The club said the 74-year-old is expected to be released in "the next day or two".

While no details were released regarding the procedure, Celtic added they "would like to thank supporters for their kind wishes".

O'Neill was named permanent boss this summer after guiding Celtic to a Premiership and Scottish Cup double last season.

He was in the dugout on Monday as Celtic kicked off their league title defence with a 1-0 win over Dundee at Parkhead.

Celtic are next in action on Sunday as they visit Kilmarnock, live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: LIV Golf reaches agreement with new 'lead investor'
Sports.content:
LIV Golf has reached an agreement with a new unnamed investor after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced in April it was ending funding to the breakaway league at the end of 2026.

Sky Sports News understands the deal is set to be finalised this month.

As part of the arrangement, players will also own a majority equity stake in the league, with the season set to be hosted around 10 annual team events.

The season schedule would also include five global "Team Majors" staged across different continents.

The PIF's decision to withdraw funding from the league in April cast doubt over LIV Golf's future.

Following a board restructuring, LIV later announced that it was seeking new "long-term financial partners".

But LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil has told Sky Sports News that along with the new investor, the league is building a new 'multi-partner model' as it looks to secure its longevity going forward.

"LIV Golf has an agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the Board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the League's next era, driven by and for the players," O'Neil said.

More to follow…

Sports.title: Reijnders and Semenyo shine in Maresca's interesting tactical set-up
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca won his first game in charge of Manchester City with a 3-1 win over the K-League All Stars in Seoul.

All four goals were scored in the opening 23 minutes as City bounced back from Saturday's penalty shoot-out loss to Inter Milan.

Rayan Ait-Nouri, Tijjani Reijnders and Divin Mubama all scored for City, who used 22 players in the win.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Maresca's first win in charge of Manchester City…

Maresca's interesting tactical set-up

How Man City lined up Starting XI: Donnarumma; Lewis, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol; Kovacic, Reijnders; Semenyo, Foden, Ait-Nouri; Mubama.

Finishing XI: Bettinelli; Nunes, Alleyne, Reis, Mfuni; Gonzalez, Heskey; Savinho, Echeverri, Monga; Marmoush.

Maresca said last month he is not a "copy and paste" coach as he looks to succeed Pep Guardiola - and his tactics in Seoul were certainly different.

Rico Lewis played at right-back, but when City were in possession he tucked infield and supported the midfield pairing of Mateo Kovacic and Reijnders.

It meant City had a three-man defence of Josko Gvardiol, Abdukodir Khusanov and Ruben Dias when in possession.

Ait-Nouri and Antoine Semenyo were the wingers and played very high and wide - and that paid off immediately as the former scored a ninth-minute opener from his left-wing position.

Phil Foden was handed a free role in the No 10 position behind striker Muamba, who scored in consecutive pre-season games.

Reijnders impresses amid Forest links

On Tuesday, reports emerged that Nottingham Forest were eyeing a £55m move for Reijnders.

But on this showing in South Korea, City will want to keep the Netherlands international.

His driving runs from deep and technical ability allowed City to create chances and dominate.

The ex-AC Milan midfielder superbly set up Ait-Nouri's opener before he restored City's lead with a fine low finish across goal from Semenyo's inventive backheel assist.

The 28-year-old faces stiff competition in midfield next season, especially after the £116m arrival of Elliot Anderson​​​​​​, who is not part of City's pre-season tour of Asia after his World Cup exertions with England.

But more performances like this will make City think twice about potentially moving Reijnders on this summer.

Semenyo shines in Seoul

Semenyo may not have scored in Seoul, but he was outstanding and City's best player.

A lively performance from the Ghana international saw him terrorise the hosts' defence.

He produced a sublime assist for Reijnders' goal and then played a huge part in Muamba's rebound finish as his shot after cutting inside was parried straight to the striker to tap home.

Semenyo was taken off at half-time and replaced by Savinho, but the Tottenham target did not reach Semenyo's levels.

The ex-Bournemouth attacker impressed in the second half of last season after joining in January, and he looks set to scale new heights under Maresca in the upcoming campaign.

Image: Man City celebrate their win over the K-League All Stars

Another quick equaliser conceded - and from City's left again

There were just three minutes between Ait-Nouri's opener and the K-League All Stars' equaliser.

That was three minutes less than what it took Inter Milan to level up on Saturday after Muamba had given City the lead over the Italian champions.

That is now two quick concessions after scoring the first goal, and this switching off is something Maresca will have taken note of.

There was further déjà vu about Dae-Won Kim's equaliser, with the goal coming down City's right side.

Benjamin Pavard's finish for Inter Milan on Saturday came after Federico Dimarco had found acres of space inside the box on City's right.

Four days on, it was the K-League All Stars who exploited City's right-hand side as Kim cut in from the left and struck an equaliser.

City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, though, would have been disappointed with the goal after being beaten at his near post.

Picking the ball out of the net was the only thing Donnarumma did in Seoul, but he will know that at the same venue this Sunday (12pm UK time) he will likely have more to do in City's next pre-season game against Atletico Madrid.

Sports.title: Luís Figo blasts ‘deceitful’ Infantino and says Fifa president must quit to ‘save football’
Sports.content:
The Portugal legend Luís Figo has described Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated scheme to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed” and called on the Fifa president to resign.

Infantino was forced to scrap his controversial proposal after a fierce backlash that was led by Uefa, with the 56-year-old now battling for his future having called an emergency meeting of Fifa staff on Wednesday as pressure on him mounts.

On Tuesday the Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, accused Fifa of blackmail by threatening to withhold financial assistance from his federation if it refused to back the president’s bid for re-election. That came after former Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger, who is Fifa’s chief of global football development, issued a statement distancing himself from the plan that said the decision to withdraw it was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”.

Figo, the former Barcelona and Real Madrid forward who won 127 caps for Portugal, has now joined the chorus of criticism and accused Infantino of having “debased the office of Fifa president that he promised to elevate” since taking over in 2016.

“I could write 10,000 words on the problems at Fifa. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go,” he wrote in the Daily Mail.

“He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve. He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the Fifa Peace Prize winner [Donald Trump]. It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Figo, who has been a football adviser to Uefa since 2017, cited Infantino’s lack of transparency over his attempts to push through the private equity deal that would have reportedly led to increase in his salary to $30m a year as more evidence that he is unfit to govern world football.

“It’s not honest when you fail to mention that, after you have delivered the head of the World Cup on a platter to your mates in DC, they are going to give you a job worth five times your current salary,” he wrote.

“None of this comes as a surprise when you consider the litany of abuses he has inflicted on football’s reputation; from suspending and reversing disciplinary decisions to breaking the laws of the game over a half-time show, nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends.”

Sports.title: ‘Dream come true’: Eva Olid delighted after being named Manchester United’s new head coach
Sports.content:
Eva Olid has described being appointed as the Manchester United Women head coach as a dream come true, after signing a two-year contract until 2028 with the option of a further year.

The Spanish coach will replace Marc Skinner, whose surprise departure was announced on Monday morning.

Olid had been out of work since guiding Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last season and leaving the Edinburgh club by mutual agreement, after a five-year spell during which she oversaw a remarkable period of progress.

The 40-year-old’s arrival comes as United are understood to be prioritising developing their own young, homegrown players rather than spending large transfer fees. In a statement the club said: “Olid’s appointment marks the start of an exciting new era for Manchester United Women as the club embarks on a clear vision for long-term, sustainable growth and success.

“Important foundations have already been put in place to further support the development of homegrown talent and young players, as well as senior internationals, and establish a clear football identity. Significant investment has been made into the academy infrastructure and facilities, underlining the ambition to build the leading youth development system in the country.”

Olid told the club’s website: “The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true. The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team, and an exceptional group of support staff.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid signs up for Manchester United. Photograph: Manchester United/Getty Images

“There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential. I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud.”

United finished fourth in the Women’s Super League last season and reached the quarter-finals of the Women’s Champions League, as well as the League Cup final.

Matt Johnson, United’s director of women’s football, said: “Eva is an outstanding coach with an incredible determination to succeed. Her remarkable achievements at Heart of Midlothian showcased her ability to maximise the potential of individual players, whilst also implementing an exciting style of football.

“Eva is the perfect coach to lead us into an exciting new era. She shares our commitment to developing exciting homegrown and young players, a tradition deeply embedded in our club’s history and culture, as well as improving established senior internationals, both of which form an integral part of our vision for long-term, sustainable success.”

Sports.title: ‘Trabzon, are you ⁠ready?’: Mohamed Salah lands in Turkey to sign for Trabzonspor
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah arrived smiling at an Istanbul airport on Wednesday wearing Trabzonspor’s burgundy and blue kit ahead of ⁠his expected move to ⁠the Turkish Super Lig ​side, as hundreds of fans jostled for a glimpse of the Egyptian forward.

Trabzonspor announced on Tuesday they were in negotiations with ⁠Salah and the club chairman, Ertugrul Dogan, said they expected to sign the 34-year-old on a free transfer at a ceremony in the Black Sea city on Thursday.

“Trabzon, are you ⁠ready? I can hear you. See you very soon,” Salah said in a video posted by the club ​on X. “Everywhere is Trabzon to us,” he added ‌while wearing a Trabzonspor kit, referring ‌to the club’s motto.

Upon arriving at Ataturk Airport, Salah was met by hundreds of fans. He waved ‌at supporters and initiated a traditional chant with them, before departing for a medical check and a later planned flight east to Trabzon.

Salah left Liverpool this summer after nine ‌years, having scored 257 goals in 442 appearances, where he won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once.

In the 2024-25 season Salah scored 29 Premier League goals and provided 18 assists, equalling the league record for most goal involvements in a season and setting the record for a 38-game campaign. He was named Premier League Player ‌of the Season and won the Golden Boot and the Playmaker Award, becoming the first player to take all three in one campaign.

His output ​waned last season, with seven goals and seven assists in 27 league matches and he was left on the bench in Champions League games, leading to a public spat with Liverpool’s then-manager Arne Slot.

The 34-year-old began his career in Europe at Swiss side Basel in 2012 and ⁠later joined Chelsea. He also had brief stints at Fiorentina and Roma between 2015 and 2017 ​before joining Liverpool.

Trabzonspor – generally ​considered to be the fourth-biggest team in Turkey after Istanbul ​sides Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, and ‌Besiktas – finished third ​in the Super Lig ​last season and will enter the Europa League playoffs.

Salah had been close to joining the Istanbul club Besiktas, whose football director Onder Ozen said negotiations had stalled over financial and image-rights demands, according to local media.

Sports.title: ‘Punch to the gut’: Indian football thrown into chaos with Jamshedpur withdrawal from ISL | John Duerden
Sports.content:
“Please don’t let this be the final whistle for Jamshedpur FC,” the defender Pratik Chaudhari said, looking into the camera as teammates looked on disconsolately. “We would like to say on behalf of all the players, please do rethink about this. Because if this happens, this is not just a loss for Indian football … this is a big loss for all of India.”

In addition, fans of the Indian Super League club marched in protest, petitions were launched, and the Indian football legend Sunil Chhetri said it was a “punch to the gut” and joined others in begging for a rethink.

The target of all these pleas was the Jamshedpur owner Tata Steel, which surprisingly pulled the plug on the club on 31 July. After the problems of the 2025-26 campaign, which started five months late and lasted just 13 games, the new season’s big kick-off on 4 September was to be a new start. The positivity and optimism before the new season, fragile though it was, disappeared along with JFC.

And understandably so as it is a huge blow, for players, staff and fans but also for the league. Jamshedpur had solid support and won the ISL shield in 2022, five years after the club was formed. Steve Coppell was the first head coach with Scott Cooper, Aidy Boothroyd and Owen Coyle all following in his footsteps.

Baljit Rihal of Inventive Sports was the agent who took Coppell to the city in the eastern state of Jharkhand. “To be quite frank, after all the uncertainty Indian football has faced over the last couple of seasons, Jamshedpur FC would have been one of the last clubs I expected to pull out,” he told the Guardian.

The club was founded by the Tata Group, which has been involved with Indian football at various levels for decades. “When an institution with that history decides it can no longer continue at the highest level, it says something very serious about the current state of the game,” Rihal said.

The league is also losing a major corporate backer, one which insists, however, that the decision is not about money. “At Tata Steel, sports have never been evaluated through a profit-and-loss lens,” the company’s vice-president and the club’s chairman, Sundara Ramam, told the Guardian.

View image in fullscreen Jamshedpur FC won the Indian Super League shield in 2022 Photograph: Courtesy of ISL

“Our decision to exit professional club football has nothing to do with Tata Steel’s financial position. In fact, the resources that would have been spent on the club will continue to be invested in grassroots sports development. Our sports budget is not decreasing. It will continue to grow. As chairman of Jamshedpur FC, I can say clearly that this decision was driven by our desire to focus more intensely on grassroots development and not by financial considerations.”

Yet if others follow suit then there may not be much of a professional pathway for young talent. This latest episode shines a light on the league once more. In the club’s original letter sent to the All India Football Federation, concerns were expressed about the financial model of the ISL, which recently changed. Reliance Industries was the federation’s commercial partner from 2010 but, when that agreement expired in 2025, a new deal was not made and a new partner not found, hence the shortened season.

This time, the AIFF looks after governance and administration with the clubs taking on the commercial and marketing side. “The old model meant clubs had very little say in how the league was packaged and sold,” Ravi Puskur, the chief executive of Goa FC, said last month.

“Now the clubs hold the broadcast and sponsorship rights directly. It puts the incentive to grow the league’s commercial value in the hands of the people who are most invested in it growing.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A member of Jamshedpur’s staff told the Guardian that the decision was because of concerns over the new arrangements. “I believe Tata are not interested in the club-led model,” he says. “There had to be a commitment of four years and the AIFF was asking for an initial payment of around £43,000 from all 14 clubs to be made by 31 July. Tata might have thought it’s better to stop rather than get dragged into unknown waters.”

View image in fullscreen The former Crystal Palace manager Steve Coppell was the club’s first head coach in 2017. Photograph: The India Today Group/Getty Images

It is a worrying exit as this is not the only corporate departure from Indian football of late. “Reliance stepping away from its central role was significant,” Rihal says. “City Football Group leaving Mumbai City was another warning.” That happened in December, in the middle of the problems last season. “Tata now withdrawing from Jamshedpur FC feels different again because of the group’s deep-rooted history in Indian football. These departures have happened for different reasons, but collectively they represent a major loss of confidence in the professional game.”

Now there is fear that others may follow and there will be some relief if all 13 remaining clubs kick off the season. “Indian football can recover, but we should not underestimate the scale of the challenge,” Rihal says.

“The priority now must be the people affected, followed by urgent clarity over the league’s structure and future. Players, staff and supporters cannot continue living from one period of uncertainty to the next. They deserve much better.”

There is still hope that Tata could have a rethink. “I understand that some tough decisions in sport are down to what makes sense in the boardroom,” Chhetri said. “But I can only request and hope that the thinktank at Tata picks their heart over head and reconsiders this call. It might be a poor business decision, but it will be the one Indian football needs the most at this hour.”

Sports.title: Continuity, chaos and Rodman: how Washington Spirit are thriving in NWSL
Sports.content:
The National Women’s Soccer League is just past the midway point of its 14th regular season, with 12 of 30 games remaining in the regular season (though half the league’s teams have one or more games in hand).

Despite a number of developments in 2026 – including two new expansion teams and the Utah Royals on a historic tear – some things have stayed consistent. At the moment, that includes a third consecutive season featuring the Washington Spirit as a top-two team. With the business end of the season looming, the mark of success is twofold: maintain that consistency through the end-of-year melee and into the playoffs (easier said than done) and, importantly for the Spirit, level up with a first-place finish in the table and/or a Championship trophy.

Continuity at the top doesn’t come easy in a league such as the NWSL. Over the years, the league has earned its reputation as a parity-based competition where – whether it be a weekend upset between teams at either end of the table, or a “worst-to-first” scenario from one season to the next – anything can happen. Teams have had years-long runs of dominant results. Most notably, the North Carolina Courage finished the regular season in first place for three consecutive seasons from 2017 to 2019, while also winning the NWSL Championship twice in that time. But over the course of 14 seasons the NWSL table has been famous for fluctuations.

Some early new trends have emerged in recent seasons. Teams such as Gotham, San Diego, Kansas City, Orlando and Washington have had a steady presence in the playoff spots (notable by NWSL standards), but their places in the top eight have varied, as has their success in the playoffs.

And yet while teams around them have had their highs and lows throughout the table (including a mercurial Gotham, one of three teams to beat Washington this season, who moved ahead of them into first place on Sunday) the Spirit have been, well, consistently good. And they’ve been good despite navigating myriad changes, including the departure of the former NWSL rookie of the year Croix Bethune – who now plays for Kansas City – and two key starters in the run to the championship last season (Aubrey Kingsbury and Casey Krueger) on maternity leave.

View image in fullscreen Croix Bethune, seen here surging away from Gotham FC’s Esther González, left Washington Spirit and joined Kansas City Current. Photograph: Reed Hoffmann/AP

“Turnover is normal in this league, so we do not take continuity for granted,” says Haley Carter, Washington’s president of soccer operations – a former player, coach and executive who most recently played a key role in Orlando Pride’s historic championship-winning season in 2024.

Describing the importance of adding the right players to a strong foundation, Carter says: “We try to be thoughtful about who joins the club. When we sign a player or hire on the sporting side, fit is one of the first things we look at, because we are trying to build an environment and not just a roster.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Spirit have done a commendable job with talent identification in recent years, and have folded international talents from a large swath of countries into the spine of their team. Last June, Sofia Cantore became the first Italian in NWSL (she finished with four goals and one assist in 12 games, and has the same number this season). They also signed the league’s first Paraguayan, the 18-year-old Claudia Martínez, who has three goals in an impressive rookie campaign.

With the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) ongoing, the Spirit have six players there representing Nigeria, Algeria, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon and Burkina Faso. (It’s a nod to the team’s depth that they’ve managed reasonably well without them.) Importantly, with Kingsbury out, the 28-year-old Scottish goalkeeper Sandy MacIver has stepped in with aplomb, setting a team record for consecutive clean sheets (four) and has the fourth-best save percentage in the league.

Of course, in addition to the Spirit’s impressive cadre of international talents, one of the NWSL’s most marketable names, Trinity Rodman, is pivotal to their past success and ongoing hopes of winning more trophies. Rodman’s 13 goal contributions in 18 games are the team’s most amid an in-form season. Her ability to press a backline, create space, take on defenders and link with teammates such as Cantore or the Colombian midfielder Leicy Santos has been inseparable from the side’s consistency this year.

View image in fullscreen Trinity Rodman (centre) slots the ball past the Houston Dash keeper Jane Campbell to score one of her two goals in Washington Spirit’s 2-1 victory in July. Photograph: Scott Taetsch/NWSL/Getty Images

With interest from abroad, Rodman’s contract was so important to the team and league that (with the investment-happy support of the team owner, Michele Kang) the NWSL created a new “high-impact player” policy to help keep her stateside. The so-called Rodman rule allows teams to spend $1m outside the standard salary cap for players who meet certain criteria.

Kang, who has made news in recent weeks because of a $400m lawsuit with John Textor, is one of the most well-known figures in women’s football, as the owner of three clubs in three countries (the Spirit, OL Lyonnes and London City Lionesses). According to Carter, collaboration among the trio is indeed under way. It is “one of the most exciting parts of what we are building” and “is more structured than people might assume”.

Rather than reinvent the wheel, the three clubs collaborate across medical, performance and technical departments, and use “shared themes, shared processes, and increasingly shared software platforms for talent identification, performance management, athlete wellness, and operational efficiency”.

While things are looking bright for the Spirit at the moment, the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs just beyond will be the final proving ground for the theme of their season thus far: despite changes and good old NWSL chaos, the Spirit can be reliably good.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £75m fee with Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães as clubs reach compromise
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães is poised to leave Newcastle’s pre-season training camp in southern Spain and fly to London before a £75m move to Arsenal. The departing Newcastle captain is scheduled to undergo a medical in north London in the next couple of days after the two clubs finally compromised on the fee.

While Arsenal had wanted initially to pay no more than £60m for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November and has two years remaining on his contract, Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80m.

Having sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively this summer, Newcastle had no need to sell Guimarães and would have preferred to keep a player who was integral to their 2025 League Cup triumph.

Since the Brazilian’s arrival from Lyon in January 2022, Newcastle have struggled to win games without Guimarães on the pitch. In his 153 league appearances he scored 30 goals, contributed 26 assists and, as Eddie Howe’s former team twice qualified for the Champions League, became an enduring crowd favourite. The loss of Guimarães is likely to hit Newcastle fans appreciably harder than even Alexander Isak’s defection to Liverpool last year.

Guimarães, though, was determined to join Arsenal even before Howe stepped down as manager last week. He flew to La Manga to meet the club’s in-coming manager, Matthias Jaissle, on Monday but is understood to have told Jaissle he wanted out and could not be persuaded otherwise. The parting is believed to have been cordial and in marked contrast to Isak’s acrimonious exit last summer.

Lyon will receive a windfall in the region of £7m because of a sell-on clause that stipulates they are entitled to 20% of any profit Newcastle make on the sale of Guimarães.

Arsenal, who have sanctioned the sale of Christian Norgaard to Everton for £7m in anticipation of bringing in Guimarães, are now expected to step up their attempts to sign a defender and another forward before the end of the transfer window. They could face competition from Liverpool in their attempts to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa because of concerns over William Saliba’s back issues that will force him to miss “an extended period”. It is thought that Villa want £60m for the England defender but Arsenal are unwilling to pay that much for a player who has less than two years of his contract remaining.

Arsenal have also registered their interest in signing Guimarães’s Brazil teammate Vinícius Júnior but are looking at alternatives should he decide to stay at Real Madrid. Barcelona’s sporting director, Deco, is expected to hold talks with Atlético Madrid over Julián Alvarez on Wednesday in a bid to secure a deal for the Argentina forward but Arsenal are hoping that the 26-year-old could yet be persuaded to join them.
