Mikel Arteta’s side have also been linked with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, who is wanted by Liverpool and valued at around £145m by the European champions.

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns in Chelsea defeat as Milan pay tribute to Baresi
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso hailed Mykhailo Mudryk’s “emotional” return from a doping ban as the winger played for Chelsea for the first time in nearly two years in a 1-0 friendly defeat by Juventus in Hong Kong on Wednesday.

Mudryk came on as a substitute for Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute, drawing applause from his teammates and loud cheers from Chelsea fans in the 43,575 crowd at Kai Tak Sports Park.

The Ukraine international has not played a competitive match since November 2024, having been provisionally suspended after returning an “adverse finding” for the banned substance meldonium. However, the 25-year-old was cleared to return to action after resolving the case with the Football Association.

Despite a lively cameo on the left side, Mudryk was unable to stop Juventus taking the spoils courtesy of a wonderful second-half strike from the Kosovo international Edon Zhegrova.

“Really pleased for him. It was emotional for everyone from the club to see him back,” Alonso said after the match. “He was thrilled, for sure. After such a long period, to be back on the pitch, it was a great feeling for him.”

Neither side could find the breakthrough in a drab first half as two experimental lineups struggled to create clearcut chances.

Danny Welbeck could have scored a goal on his first appearance in a Chelsea shirt but the veteran England striker failed to direct a flicked header on target.

Early in the second half a long ball from Moisés Caicedo put the new signing Marco Palestra in on goal but his tame shot could not beat Mattia Perin.

Juventus finally broke the deadlock with a moment of magic in the 68th minute, Kenan Yildiz squaring for Zhegrova who curled a stunning strike into the top corner from outside the box.

Both sides rang the changes but Chelsea could not find a cutting edge. “I think we started pretty well,” Alonso said. “The first 30, 35 minutes, we have played with good control, we have created a few chances. And the second half, there were many changes. The game was not that controlled and stable with all the substitutions.

“Unluckily we didn’t get to win, but for sure it’s the process, it’s minutes for everyone.”

Chelsea will play Milan in Jakarta on Saturday, before rounding off preseason with games against Malaysia’s Johor Darul Ta’zim and Spain’s Real Sociedad.

View image in fullscreen Milan and Inter players pay tribute to Franco Baresi in Perth. Photograph: Richard Wainwright/AAP

Christopher Nkunku converted a late penalty as Milan salvaged a draw with Inter in a lacklustre preseason derby on Wednesday in Perth. The match was the first for Milan since the death of Franco Baresi, who captained the club during a golden era in the 1980s and 1990s. There was a minute’s silence before the match with players from both teams linking arms.

In front of 52,310 fans in Australia, the Serie A champions Inter appeared to be claiming the bragging rights after Federico Dimarco’s strike from close range in the 52nd minute. But Nkunku was brought down by Carlos Augusto in the 83rd minute before squaring the contest with a superbly taken penalty.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Coventry to make Yirenkyi new record signing, Palace swoop for Gozo
Sports.content:
Coventry are set to break their transfer record for the fourth time in this window after agreeing a £23m fee with Danish side Nordsjælland for the Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi.

The deal for Yirenkyi, who impressed during the Black Stars’ World Cup campaign and scored the winning goal against Panama in the group stage, is set to be a record for the Danish top flight and comes after Coventry have already spent almost £60m on the winger Loum Tchaouna, the defender Aurèle Amenda and the goalkeeper Carl Rushworth. Yirenkyi, who was named young player of the year in the Danish league last season, will travel to Coventry in the coming hours to complete his move.

The 20-year-old is a product of the Right to Dream academy in Ghana and has been with Nordsjælland since 2024. It is understood that the Coventry manager, Frank Lampard, has spoken to his former Chelsea teammate Michael Essien, who is now working as a coach at Nordsjælland, about what Yirenkyi could bring to his newly promoted side. Brighton and Everton have also been linked with him in the past.

Elsewhere, Crystal Palace are closing in on the signing of the USA youth international Zavier Gozo as their new manager, Pierre Sage, attempts to strengthen his squad ahead of the new season.

Gozo, a 19-year-old who plays for Real Salt Lake in MLS and has represented the USA at various youth levels up to under-23, is expected to complete an £11m move to south London after he was left out of his side’s game on Tuesday night owing to an “excused absence”.

It is understood Palace have tracked Gozo’s progress at Real Salt Lake – who are part-owned by David Blitzer, the American who is one of Palace’s co-owners – for some time and view him as a potential successor to Daniel Muñoz at right wing-back. Palace need cover after Nathaniel Clyne’s departure at the end of his contract and selling Danny Imray to Wrexham for a fee that is thought to have been in the region of £5m last week.

View image in fullscreen Zavier Gozo is seen as a potential successor to Daniel Muñoz at Selhurst Park. Photograph: Anne-Marie Sorvin/USA Today Sports

Sage is also hoping to bring in several more players before the end of the transfer window as Palace prepare to juggle their Premier League challenge with a Europa League campaign, with a particular focus on replacing Maxence Lacroix after the France defender’s departure to Chelsea. Axel Disasi, who spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham, is one option, while Palace have also been in talks with Brest over the teenage centre-back Raphaël Le Guen. Negotiations with Augsburg – the German club where Blitzer also owns a stake – over the French defender Chrislain Matsima broke down last week.

Palace are also thought to be targeting another forward and midfielder but are determined not to sell any of their leading players, including Adam Wharton, who has interest from Chelsea. The former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been training with Palace in pre-season as he aims to earn a move after leaving Ajax, with his fellow Japan international Daichi Kamada signing a one-year contract extension last month.

Palace are also expected to offer Ismaïla Sarr a new deal to ward off interest from Fenerbahce in the Senegal forward, who scored 21 goals last season. Club Brugge have had an initial offer for Romain Esse rejected but the Belgian side are expected to return with an improved bid for the England Under-21 forward.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are close to agreeing a £16.3m deal to sign the defender Pep Chavarría from Rayo Vallecano. The 28-year-old, who was part of the team that reached last season’s Conference League final, is a left-sided defender and will provide competition for Jorrel Hato following the departure of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid.

Bournemouth are finalising a £11m deal for the Sevilla right-back Juanlu Sánchez. Juanlu, who is expected to sign a four-year contract, will represent the third summer signing since Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola, joining Álvaro Rodríguez and Antonio Silva at the club who signed from Elche and Benfica respectively.

Manchester United are selling Radek Vitek to Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £14m as his fellow goalkeeper Altay Bayindir prepares to join Celta Vigo on loan.

Michael Carrick’s side are in the process of shaping their squad for the new season, with their No 1, Senne Lammens, joined by the summer signing Karl Darlow in a new-look goalkeeping department. Vitek is on the verge of joining Boro, the defeated Championship playoff finalists, following an impressive season with Bristol City.

Sports.title: Henry Pollock the million-pound player? Why Eddie Hearn's sums don't add up, the reality of the French threat and how this will all likely end
Sports.content:
When Henry Pollock became the first rugby player to sign with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency in March, it was a positive shift for the sport.

The English club game has struggled financially and its players have, with a few exceptions, struggled to cut through into mainstream society. Hearn’s arrival into the game was viewed as a means of changing that, raising the profiles of Pollock and Scotland No 10 Finn Russell who also joined the stable and by extension, that of rugby too. It all seemed rather positive.

Almost immediately, however, Hearn questioned how much Pollock was earning through his contracts with club Northampton Saints and England. He vowed to soon increase that.

On Monday, Hearn went one step further. He told The Daily Telegraph that Pollock, still just 21 and with a grand total of one start for England under his belt, was deserving of a Northampton salary of £1million a year.

This was on the basis that he is a player who brings a unique combination of undoubted on-field talent as well as significant commercial benefits to the sport he plays. ‘He's certainly a seven-figure player,’ Hearn said. ‘The way rugby's going and what Pollock is doing, his value over the next couple of years will skyrocket and I think the value of rugby will.’

Hearn is right about one thing. Pollock has been a breath of fresh air to English rugby. He is supremely talented and although not universally popular, he is exactly the sort of player the sport needs to grow. Where Hearn is misguided, however, is on the numbers.

When Henry Pollock became the first rugby player to sign with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency in March, it was a positive shift for the sport

Pollock has been a breath of fresh air to English rugby. He is supremely talented and although not universally popular, he is exactly the sort of player the sport needs to grow

Pollock’s current Northampton contract – which, and the timing is crucial to Hearn's words, expires next summer – is worth £150,000 and his status as an Enhanced Elite Playing Squad (EEPS) member with England also earns him roughly the same again from the RFU.

But in English rugby’s current financial climate, it is simply inconceivable for Northampton – or indeed any of the other nine PREM Rugby teams – to pay Pollock such a sum. Even with the investment coming into the league, the money just does not exist in this country right now.

It would great if it did as it would reflect significant growth across the English game. But, unfortunately, it does not. It is pie in the sky. The only possible side who could go to such lengths is Newcastle Red Bulls following their takeover by the energy drink giants, though that is unlikely.

Even the richest French clubs, in their thriving system full of money, would likely baulk at such a figure - and, of course, would require Pollock to give up his England career by playing overseas.

Antoine Dupont, still the biggest star in the world game, earns £1.2million a year at Toulouse, but Pollock is not on the France scrum-half's level, in talent or earnings power. England heavyweights Owen Farrell and Maro Itoje would have earned close to £1million at Saracens - but that was before the EEPS contracts came in, where the RFU covers some of the player's salary to lower the burden on clubs.

But really, it is irrelevant. Pollock does not want to leave Northampton. It is also pointless Hearn comparing Pollock’s income with that of his boxing clients. It is like comparing chalk with cheese. Rugby, unfortunately, remains far behind boxing and miles off football in terms of the wealth within the sport.

There is no doubt that Pollock’s rapid ascent from an academy player to a regular England international and British & Irish Lion is unusual for one so young. As such, he is certainly deserving of an increase from £150,000.

But Hearn’s demands are likely to cause a problem for Northampton. All PREM teams are limited to a playing squad spend of £6.4m, with the salary of one ‘marquee’ player allowed outside that figure. Northampton are a club who do not spend up to the maximum in a bid to ensure financial stability, making their league titles in 2024 and 2026 all the more impressive.

There is no doubt that Pollock’s rapid ascent to a regular England international and British & Irish Lion is unusual for one so young. He is certainly deserving of an increase

Northampton do not spend close to the PREM Rugby salary cap, which makes their recent titles in 2024 and 2026 all the more impressive

It is unlikely that the Saints hierarchy of director of rugby Phil Dowson and chief executive Julia Chapman will blow their team’s modus operandi into smithereens at Hearn’s demands, even if they will clearly want to keep hold of Pollock. They have other high-class England stars to keep happy too, namely Fin Smith, Tommy Freeman and Alex Mitchell.

Another complication is that when Pollock and Russell announced their Matchroom deals, it was confirmed that their then-representative Matt Hart of Stellar Group, would remain in charge of their playing contracts.

That is still the case. But Hearn’s comments do raise an interesting question as to who will be leading the negotiating with Northampton. Hearn and Hart are working collaboratively with Pollock, but the former’s comments have certainly rocked the boat.

The likely result of all this is a compromise. Pollock will get an increase, though it is almost certain to fall well short of Hearn’s demands. The player, however, is likely to in time get close to being the million-pound man through additional commercial contracts alongside his Northampton and England deals. And that can only be a good thing for him and rugby as a whole.

Sports.title: Aston Villa braced for fresh Arsenal bid for Ezri Konsa, Mikey Moore set for Cologne loan... and Mo Salah jets in to Turkey: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Spurs yet to approach Liverpool about Gakpo

Tottenham remain keen to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool, as reported earlier this week, but, as of this afternoon, the Reds have yet to receive a formal approach.

Liverpool want to keep Gakpo but are exploring the possibility of signing Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain as well as Bradley Barcola. But they are not in for Pedro Neto at Chelsea, who is a target for Manchester City

Liverpool do not want to sell Cody Gakpo, with Spurs interested in a move

Toon working on replacement for Bruno

Newcastle are working to find a replacement for Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to have a medical at Arsenal after a £75m deal was agreed.

They have asked about Dortmund's Felix Nmecha, Angelo Stiller at Stuttgart and Luka Sucic at Real Sociedad, among others. as they try to find a solution swiftly with new boss Matthias Jaissle being announced tonight

Melia hopes to impress at the Imps

Tottenham’s teenage striker Mason Melia has undergone his medical at Lincoln today ahead of finalising his loan move. The 18-year-old is a Republic of Ireland international.

Spurs' Moore set for Germany

Tottenham winger Mikey Moore is poised to accept a loan move to Cologne in Germany.

The 18-year-old spent last year on loan with Rangers.

Mikey Moore is set for another second loan spell after spending last year at Rangers

Villa working on £14m Ruggeri deal

Aston Villa are continuing to discussing a £14m deal with Atletico Madrid for Italian left-back Matteo Ruggeri but they are awaiting approval from the 24-year-old. Daily Mail Sport reported their interest yesterday.

Atletico looking to utilise funds towards their planned bid for Cristian Romero at Tottenham.

Burnley go for keeper Amos

Burnley have signed free agent goalkeeper Ben Amos.

The 36-year-old had taken part in the PFA training camp for free agents this summer after leaving Port Vale at the end of last season. He has signed a one-year deal with Burnley.

Amos has over 360 appearances with a host of EFL clubs after beginning his career at Manchester United.

Ben Amos spent time at Charlton, among several EFL clubs

Chalobah arrives for Como medical

Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah has arrived in Italy for his medical with Como. The deal is worth an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons.

Trevoh Chalobah is closing in on a move to Como

Coventry aim to break transfer record AGAIN

Coventry are attempting to break their transfer record for the second time this week after offering nearly £26million for Ghana star Caleb Yirenkyi.

The midfielder, who plays for Danish club Nordsjaelland, represented his country at this summer’s World Cup as they drew 0-0 with England and exited at the first knockout stage.

Back in the top flight for the first time in 25 years, the Sky Blues have already signed goalkeeper Carl Rushworth for £22.5m as well as defender Aurele Amenda and winger Loum Tchaouna. They have also turned on-loan midfielder Frank Onyeka’s move from Brentford into a permanent switch.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Caleb Yirenkyi featured for Ghana against England in the 0-0 draw at the World Cup

Arsenal set to come back for Konsa

Aston Villa are braced for a fresh bid from Arsenal for England defender Ezri Konsa amid attempts to tie him to a new contract.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that Konsa was the Gunners’ top target for central defence though their initial proposal was well below Villa’s £60million valuation of the 28-year-old.

Konsa has remained on Arsenal’s radar since. He has two years remaining on his current deal at Villa Park and the club would like him to sign a new one.

Having already seen key men Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans depart this summer, and with Lucas Digne poised to join Paris Saint-Germain, Villa boss Unai Emery would have an even bigger rebuilding job were Konsa to depart.

Having recouped more than £140million for Rogers, who joined Chelsea, and Tielemans, who signed for Manchester United, Villa are not under financial pressure to sell Konsa and are unlikely to do so without a high-level replacement lined up.

But along with Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, Konsa is a key target for Arsenal – especially with William Saliba facing a lengthy injury absence – and they are unlikely to give up hope.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa would join England team-mate Declan Rice if Arsenal can pull off a deal

Come in No 61! Salah on his way to Turkey

Mohamed Salah is travelling to Turkey ahead of negotiating final details to complete his free transfer to Trabzonspor.

The Turkish club have posted pictures and videos on social media of the former Liverpool forward in a Trabzonspor shirt wearing No 61 while on their private plane.

Salah is scheduled to arrive in Istanbul shortly before heading to Trabzon later on today.

Read more on this story HERE

Mo Salah is pictured in a Trabzonspor shirt ahead of his move to Turkey

£14m Vitek set for Boro

Manchester United have agreed a deal worth £14million with Middlesbrough for goalkeeper Radek Vitek.

The fee is inclusive of bonuses for the highly-rated 22-year-old and there is also a 35pc sell-on clause plus matching rights and a buy back option for the Czech.

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips, 21, is also in talks over a move to Boro.

Kim Hellberg has brought in seven signings so far this summer, including Will Lankshear from Spurs in a deal worth up to £20m.

Meanwhile, two Boro players are due to have medicals ahead of moves away. Delano Burgzorg is heading to Preston in a £2m deal and Kaly Sene is joining Young Boys in Switzerland.

Bruno set for £75m Arsenal move

Arsenal are set to complete their protracted £75million move for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Full agreement is now almost done, with the clubs agreeing a compromise to end the saga.

Guimaraes is waiting for permission to leave Newcastle's training base in La Manga, in Spain, to finalise the formalities of his move to Emirates Stadium.

Read more on this story HERE

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wave goodbye to Newcastle after four years at the club

Swansea's Wilson heads to Gent

Swansea City forward Kyrell Wilson has joined KAA Gent for an undisclosed fee, subject to the relevant clearance.

The 21-year-old former Chelsea academy graduate impressed on loan at Falkirk last season and links up with the top-flight Belgian side who secured European qualification last term.

Swansea, meanwhile, are close to agreeing a deal worth £5.2m for Valencia attacking midfielder Andre Almeida.

Talks are focusing on an initial fee of £3m, plus £2.2m in add-ons as well as a sell-on clause.

Almeida, 26, was left out of Valencia’s training yesterday and has still to agree personal terms with the Welsh club.

Kyrell Wilson (left) in action for Falkirk last season - he will now head to Belgium

Altay's off to Spain

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir has been given permission to travel to Spain and complete his move to Celta Vigo.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday, the Turkey international is joining on an initial loan with option to buy around £3.5million.

Vigo will cover Bayindir salary in full and there are various performance-related bonuses.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino prepares to fight for his presidency in crunch Morocco summit just hours after Luis Figo called for under fire boss to quit - and even FIFA 'legends' are refusing to back him
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino prepares to fight for his presidency in crunch Morocco summit just hours after Luis Figo called for under fire boss to quit - and even FIFA 'legends' are refusing to back him

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA president Gianni Infantino arrived at a crunch meeting in Morocco amid mounting pressure, after football legend Luis Figo became the latest high-profile individual to call for him to resign.

Infantino had summoned senior FIFA officials to the Moroccan city of Sale for crisis talks after plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition – including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and CONCACAF – the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean – are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Pressure grew further after Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein accused him of blackmail, becoming the first Asian nation to rebel against the FIFA president.

Jordan became the 91st member association to move against Infantino, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino arrived at an emergency meeting in Sale, Morocco on Wednesday

Infantino is facing mounting pressure over his failed plan to sell off stakes in the FIFA World Cup

Football legend Luis Figo became the latest high-profile individual to call for him to resign, while Arsene Wenger distanced himself from Infantino's plans

A car carrying Infantino was seen arriving at FIFA's Africa regional office in Sale on Wednesday.

The meeting comes hours after Figo became the latest major name in football to demand his resignation.

In an explosive piece for Daily Mail Sport, which will further ramp up the pressure on the under-fire FIFA chief, the Portuguese legend described his now aborted World Cup sell-off as the ‘lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed’ and a ‘grubby, underhand plot’.

Across 600 no-holds-barred words Figo, who had initially backed Infantino in 2015, brands the disgraced exec a ‘relic who should have no part in football’s future’ and accuses him of ‘a litany of abuses’, also referencing the now-infamous suspension of the ban behind Folarin Balogun’s red card and the half-time show at the World Cup final which ‘broke the laws of the game’.

‘Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate,’ the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Inter Milan star writes. ‘He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.’

Figo, now 53, is viewed by many as a potential successor to Aleksandr Ceferin, head of UEFA which is leading the war against Infantino.

Figo and Jordan's Prince Ali had both previously stood against former FIFA president Sepp Blatter in the 2015 elections.

Figo ultimately withdrew from the process, while Prince Ali pulled out after the second round of voting. Blatter announced his resignation four days after re-election amid a vast backlash.

Infantino is facing his own backlash following his World Cup plans, with FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour saying he was ‘deceived’ by the project and others, including chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, have distanced themselves from the hastily dropped plan.

Figo branded Infantino as a ‘relic who should have no part in football’s future’ in an explosive article for Daily Mail Sport

Figo, who had initially backed Infantino in 2015, claimed the Swiss official has 'debased the office of FIFA President'

With morale among staff said to be ‘rock bottom’ according to insiders, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom sent an internal email to staff citing ‘a sad and reproachable series of events’ and perhaps tellingly pointing out that ‘individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go’.

Figo, a former FIFA presidential candidate, starts: ‘I could write 10,000 words on the problems at FIFA. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go.’

He adds: ‘I have loved football all my life. I was a professional player for 20 years. And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game. But what I have seen exposed in the last ten days is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed. The man who would do that - the man who would try to force through such major changes just to enrich himself and his friends - is a relic of the game’s past and should have no part in its future.’

The Portuguese, who won 127 caps for his country, then rounds on Infantino for a lack of transparency. ’If it was such a good idea, why not tell your members when you had them all in a room before the World Cup Final?’ he asks.

‘If it was such a robust plan, why not tell your members the risks as well as what you describe as the benefits?

‘If the scheme was a no-brainer, why not be honest about the fact that it was going to give you a $30m a year job at the end of it?’

Figo adds: ‘None of this was done. Because it’s not a good idea. It’s not robust when you fail to be transparent about the crippling returns that private equity always seek.

‘It’s not bold when you fail to explain that once you have sold your share it is gone forever and you have disinherited your successors from ownership of the World Cup.

FIFA legends have reportedly declined to publicly support Infantino amid the backlash to his plans

‘And it’s not honest when you fail to mention that, after you have delivered the head of the World Cup on a platter to your mates in DC, they are going to give you a job worth five times your current salary.’

Figo then highlights FIFA’s staggering level of wealth, asking how many shares the $5billion in its reserves ‘could buy in this grubby, underhand plot’.

‘Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate,’ he writes. ‘He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve…he should go. Now.’

According to The Times, allies of Infantino had been trying to persuade 'FIFA legends' to publicly support Infantino, but have been unsuccessful.

The FIFA legends are among former international players who have been paid to appear at the governing body's events.

Sports.title: What we learned from Mykhailo Mudryk's first Chelsea appearance in two years, the 'devastating' new combination that will terrorise defences and why Xabi Alonso was left frustrated in defeat by Juventus
Sports.content:
What we learned from Mykhailo Mudryk's first Chelsea appearance in two years, the 'devastating' new combination that will terrorise defences and why Xabi Alonso was left frustrated in defeat by Juventus

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

It was in the 74th minute of this friendly loss to Juventus when Mykhailo Mudryk finally stood up from Chelsea’s bench, sent to warm-up on his own.

A little loneliness was nothing new for the Ukrainian. He grew used to training in solitary while suspended from football for the last 600 days.

Manager Xabi Alonso had already made 11 substitutions by this stage – four at half-time, and another seven after 65 minutes – and we were unsure whether we would see the 25-year-old on a field for the first time since his last appearance away at Heidenheim on November 28, 2024.

Then suddenly, it all changed. Suddenly, Alonso called him over and told him to get stripped. Suddenly, all of his Chelsea team-mates were applauding as he was introduced in the 80th minute. Suddenly, he was a footballer again, pointing to the heavens as he entered the pitch.

It is hard to fathom how Mudryk must have been feeling inside. Wearing No 43 on his back – Cole Palmer took the No 10 during his suspension with the Ukraine international’s blessing – he also wore a fine poker face. There were not too many emotions being exhibited on the outside.

Yet this is what he had been working towards. Hiring the pitch of seventh-tier Uxbridge to train on. Performing sprint sessions at the Battersea Park running track. Playing padel to mix it up. Paying to work with a personal trainer daily.

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after coming off the bench against Juventus in Hong Kong

The Ukrainian, suspended after failing a drugs test, gave glimpses of the speed still being there, reaching one ball which otherwise appeared to be rolling behind for a goal-kick

That he was allowed to even appear against Juventus is a testament to how he kept himself fit while suspended in the hope of playing again as soon as possible.

Football-wise, Mudryk gave glimpses of the speed still being there, reaching one ball which otherwise appeared to be rolling behind for a goal-kick. His first touch as a player again was cheered by the Kai Tak Stadium crowd, though it was not the greatest, his pass inside giving away possession.

Rustiness is only to be expected. Those clubs who have already approached Chelsea to ask about their plans for him for the next season – as reported by Daily Mail Sport days ago – will understand patience is needed. The most important takeaway is that this £89million signing is now back.

Mudryk has always insisted that he has no idea how the banned substance meldonium entered his system. Chelsea believe him. It was understood to have happened while away with the Ukraine national team in September 2024.

Mudryk’s return to football was made possible because of a change in the way the World Anti-Doping Agency measures meldonium. He reached a resolution with the FA because, were that same sample tested today, he would not have reported a positive test.

This return in Hong Kong was a long-time coming for Mudryk – a little light after so long in the loneliness of the shadows.

Chelsea have struck an agreement to sign the left back Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano, for £16.3million plus add-ons. He’s 28 years old, and was still playing in Spain’s second division at 24. It’s a nice story.

The Spaniard, who can also be used as a wing back, should be announced soon after travelling to London to finalise the transfer.

Marco Palestra, the right back Chelsea signed from Atalanta last month, is already impressing with the Blues

We will need to wait to assess Chavarria’s attributes, but their other defensive signing this summer, in right full back Marco Palestra, is already impressing. We say ‘defensive’. He is as attacking as a defender can be. Palestra was the fastest player in Serie A last season, and uses that pace devastatingly.

Moises Caicedo has shown how well he can play passes over the top, and with the relentlessly rapid Palestra looking to burst in behind on repeat, that could be a winning combination for Chelsea. The Italian nearly scored from one such scenario at the Kai Tak Stadium.

Despite significant speculation, Chelsea insiders insist they have not made enquiries for Porto goalkeeper Diogo Costa, and are happy heading towards the new season with Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders, who has returned after a loan with sister side Strasbourg.

Sanchez played the first 45 minutes, denying former Chelsea player Jeremie Boga from distance as it remained goalless at half-time. Penders played the second 45, conceding to a 20-yard curler from Edon Zhegrova which was beyond his reach. You simply had to applaud it as a sublime strike.

Chelsea players will now have some downtime in Hong Kong on Thursday, before then flying to Jakarta on Friday and facing another Italian side in AC Milan on Saturday.

Chelsea insiders have denied the club have enquired about Porto goalkeeper Diogo Costa, with the Blues happy to go into the season with Robert Sanchez (pictured) and Mike Penders

In Chelsea's midfield was a 16-year-old named Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, who has enjoyed tremendous exposure in this pre-season.

The England Under-17 international never shied away from wanting possession next to Caicedo, though this was yet another poor surface to play on.

A bobbling ball did not aid the football which Alonso is trying to implement, and you have to wonder whether the money involved in visiting Australia and Asia is worth the trade-off of such shoddy pitches. It cannot help preparations with the Premier League around the corner.

A poor pitch at the Kai Tak Stadium didn't help new boss Xabi Alonso's efforts to implement his style of play

Danny Welbeck started on his first appearance after arriving from Brighton. With the 35-year-old holding the ball up nicely as Chelsea’s striker, that saw Joao Pedro moved to the No 10 position.

Nicolas Jackson replaced Welbeck at half-time. It was the Senegalese who was removed when Mudryk was introduced, though that was pre-planned. Jackson had played well, but agreed to make way so that could Mudryk could have his moment. Jackson's future remains in the air this summer - Chelsea’s valuation of him is £65m.

Chelsea named 21 substitutes for this friendly. That was without Palmer or Levi Colwill, who both had minor issues and were not risked by Alonso.

While there were a fair few academy representatives on that bench, it acted as a reminder that Chelsea still need to do some selling and loaning this summer.

Sports.title: The clues Enzo Maresca gave away in Man City's K-League cruise: The new ways he wants this team to play, who's ready to start... and who isn't
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca will hope that Seoul’s searing and suffocating heat – the extent of which has seen local government advise residents to stay indoors – will fast-track the fitness of Manchester City’s squad before their season starts a week on Sunday.

A 3-1 victory over the K-League All Stars was noticeable for patterns that Maresca is trying to implement and the structures his new players need to work in.

But question marks do loom over key areas of the pitch as Daily Mail Sport looks at how the first proper week of the post-Pep Guardiola era is shaping up.

Manchester City cruised to a 3-1 win over the Korean League All Stars, scoring all three goals in the opening quarter of the match

Enzo Maresca will hope that Seoul’s searing and suffocating heat will fast-track the fitness of Manchester City’s squad before their season starts a week on Sunday

Kovacic stakes his claim

Mateo Kovacic was bullish about his future this week, claiming he never had the feeling from City’s hierarchy that a departure was in the offing this summer despite interest from elsewhere.

That throws up an intriguing conundrum around Maresca’s midfield options. With £116million club-record signing Elliot Anderson set to link up with the squad ahead of the Community Shield next weekend, and a move for Lille’s 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi progressing, the numbers are beginning to look crowded.

Kovacic would have appeared an obvious candidate to move on but he has been utilised as the deep-lying No6 in both of the friendlies so far – notably ahead of Nico Gonzalez.

Gonzalez has had the summer off after not being involved in Spain’s World Cup triumph, while Kovacic was Stateside with Croatia. Sources suggested at the end of last season that City would listen to offers for Gonzalez, who joined from Porto for £50million in January 2025.

Kovacic was replaced by Gonzalez at half-time of this win, with Tijjani Reijnders kept on for just over an hour amid interest from Nottingham Forest surrounding a £55million transfer. Reijnders has much to prove in the Premier League and his main characteristics – a strong ball-carrier who crashes into the box late – should make him an asset in the division.

While mindful of the level of opposition, he did himself no harm on Wednesday. An assist for Rayan Ait-Nouri’s opener came from Reijnders taking up a dangerous position in the right-hand channel – clearly an intentional tactic by Maresca.

His goal, swivelling first time to find the far corner following good work by Rico Lewis and Antoine Semenyo, was not the sort of action often seen in his debut campaign. But the manager was not exactly unequivocal about the Dutchman’s future.

Mateo Kovacic would have appeared an obvious candidate to move on but he has been utilised as the deep-lying No6 in both of the friendlies so far – notably ahead of Nico Gonzalez

Rayan Ait-Nouri gave City the lead inside nine minutes at the Seoul World Cup Stadium

Tijjani Reijnders, who has been linked with a £55million move to Nottingham Forest, put City back in front on 20 minutes with a low strike

‘He is here with us,’ Maresca said. ‘The players that are with us until the day that they aren't with us, it's my duty to do the best for them. I'm happy with his performance and he's working good since he came back from his holiday. At the moment I'm very happy with him.’

City will have big decisions to make on Reijnders and others in the coming weeks – even if Rodri is granted his Real Madrid wish.

Divin intervention

There are a number of clubs in the Championship weighing up loan offers for striker Divin Mubama, who scored his second poacher’s finish of pre-season when mopping up a saved Semenyo effort.

The 21-year-old West Ham academy product scored five times on loan at Stoke City last term and his role leading from the front gave some clues on how Maresca might want to deploy Erling Haaland.

City pressed with more intensity than expected, given the humidity meant the 35°C heat had a 'real feel' of 45°C. That came in the form of a 4-2-4 system, with Phil Foden up alongside Mubama.

Foden, though, was the one tasked with leading the closing down. Mubama dropped in deeper to something resembling a No10 position, sitting on the K-League midfield. That gave Foden more room and freedom to head off the press, with the rest following, and plays into his skillset.

Mubama, who is insisting that Maresca’s arrival represents a ‘fresh start’, is more adept at hunting down possession high up the pitch than Haaland, who can then serve a purpose by blocking off the passing lanes.

Divin Mubama turns in his second goal of pre-season to give City a 3-1 lead

Mubama's positioning as a No10 gave Phil gave Foden more room and freedom to head off the press, with the rest following

Wing wonders

New father Jeremy Doku is still to come back from the World Cup and will arrive as the premier winger at the club – but the fight for who earns starts on the other flank seems one-sided at the moment.

Semenyo has described Maresca’s philosophy as music to his ears, revealing how he was always struck by the clear instructions of Chelsea’s wide men to stay high.

The Ghana international has caught the eye in recent days, with that direct style favoured by his new boss. He’s done it off both flanks too, and wants to add a touch more mystery to his game.

Separate bits of ingenuity and power, showing off both sides of his talent, were meaningful contributions to a couple of City’s three goals. Both of those came shortly after Gianluigi Donnarumma was beaten at his near post by Kim Dae-won’s equaliser from the edge of the box. The Italian will hope to get those mistakes out of the way now.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo shows off his incredible supercar collection: Footballer, 41, flaunts his 'toys' after admitting he's lost count of how many he owns after developing obsession
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo showed off his jaw-dropping car collection on Instagram after previously admitting he has lost count of the number of exclusive motors he has purchased for his one-of-a-kind garage.

In a picture carousel shared to Instagram, Ronaldo allowed fans a glimpse of just some of the motors he owns with the understated caption: 'my toys (rocket emoji)'.

Among those pictured in the most recent look are a raft of Ferraris including a Purosangue, priced at £312,000, a Ferrari 599 GTO (priced at over £500,000), a Ferrari SP3 Daytona, which is worth around £1.73million, and a stunning Ferrari Monza SP1 - a rare model which has reached auction prices of nearly £2.27m.

Also in the collection pictured are two Bugattis: a £2m Veyron and an ultra-rare Centodieci, of which only 10 were ever made by the Italian constructor.

In February 2025, RM Sotheby's sold a Centodieci for a staggering estimate of £12.5m, with the limited edition car able to reach 240mph and named as one of the most expensive in the world.

Ronaldo also allowed fans a look at his McLaren Speedtail which can fetch up to £2.1m, and a Mercedes AMG One, a hybrid hypercar priced at an upwards of £2.2m.

Cristiano Ronaldo posed with just some of his collection of super and hypercars on Instagram

The Al-Nassr superstar captioned the post 'my toys' after becoming football's first billionaire

These cars represent just a handful of those owned by the Al-Nassr superstar, who opened up on his collection in an interview with Piers Morgan last year.

'If I had to bet I’d honestly say (I have) 40 or 41,' Ronaldo said. 'Honestly I don’t know. I love the Bugattis, they are different beasts.'

The 41-year-old, who was announced as football's first billionaire in 2025, also admitted that he bought a £3.2m Bugatti Tourbillon as 'an investment' rather than for pleasure.

Other supercars owned by 'CR7' are a Mercedes G-Wagon Brabus worth £600,000, which was a present to Ronaldo from his partner Georgina Rodriguez.

He also has a Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG worth £200,000, a bright orange McLaren MP4-12C (£200,000) and a Lamborghini Aventador (£270,000).

In 2021, Ronaldo bought a Bentley Flying Spur worth £250,000 to use in Manchester, having re-joined United from Juventus in August.

Ronaldo's most expensive car is a limited-edition Bugatti Centodieci - he is believed to be one of only 10 people worldwide who owns the supercar

The five-time Champions League winner bought a Ferrari Monza SP2 after visiting Ferrari HQ in Maranello in May 2021

Ronaldo's partner Georgina Rodriguez also gifted him a Rolls-Royce Dawn worth more than £250,000

Join the discussion Is Ronaldo's collection impressive or over the top?

He then purchased a £200,000 Aston Martin DBS Superleggera convertible which boasts a 5.2 litre twin-turbocharged V12 engine and is capable of delivering a stunning 715 bhp.

Ronaldo also has a Bentley Continental GT, a Lamborghini Urus and a Chevrolet Camaro worth 'only' £40,000, which is used for the family.

Rodriguez also splashed out on a third Rolls Royce for his 36th birthday - complimenting the two he already had: a Cullinan worth £300,000 and a Phantom Drophead coupe which costs around £500,000.

Rodriguez's purchase of the Rolls Royce Dawn model is understood to have cost around £500,000.

The Portugal star also told Morgan that the Al-Nassr squad are each gifted a BMW due to the manufacturer's partnership with the Saudi Pro League club.

He said he had to drive it home after a training session - a rare occasion for the forward who says he rarely gets behind the wheel in Saudi Arabia due to the high volume of traffic.

Ronaldo is currently enjoying his summer break ahead of rejoining the Al-Nassr squad and is thought to be set to marry his long-time fiancee Rodriguez in the coming weeks.

The couple have both shown off their huge diamond rings in the lead up to the apparent wedding after flying to Portugal, where they are believed to be preparing to celebrate their nuptials on Ronaldo's home island of Madeira.

Sports.title: Serena Williams, 44, steps up surprise tennis return ahead of US Open as she confirms doubles date with sister Venus, 46
Sports.content:
Serena Williams is putting her Wimbledon injury behind her to once again step up her surprise return to tennis at the ripe old age of 44.

The American icon, who has 23 majors in an incredible career, has confirmed she will participate in the women's doubles alongside her sister Venus, 46, at the upcoming Cincinnati Open.

Organizers of the event announced this week that the legendary pair have been given a wild-card entry into the doubles field of the event which takes place in Ohio next week.

Serena's return to the court increases the possibility that she will appear at another US Open this year, with that tournament taking place in New York later this month.

Venus and Serena last played a doubles match together at the 2022 US Open, and this will be their first time teaming up in the hard-court tune-up tournament in Mason, Ohio.

The Williams sisters received a wild-card entry to play doubles at Wimbledon in June, but an injury to Serena prevented that from happening. They have won 14 major titles and three Olympic gold medals in doubles play.

Serena (left) and Venus (right) Williams, pictured in 2022, are returning to the court together

Serena played at Wimbledon but injury forced her to pull out of the doubles with sister Venus

Venus Williams, 46, is also set to play mixed doubles at the US Open later this month alongside Alexander Bublik.

Serena's grass-court comeback earlier this year consisted of only three matches: a first-round win in the doubles at Queen's with Victoria Mboko – after which they had to pull out because the 19-year-old Canadian suffered an MCL knee injury – a defeat in Berlin alongside Karolina Muchova, and then a 6-3, 6-7, 6-3 loss to Maya Joint on Centre Court in the Wimbledon first round.

It was in the latter of those matches that Serena suffered a knee injury which ended any hopes of her playing alongside Venus in the women's doubles.

'I’m heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles,' she said in a post on Instagram. 'Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn’t ready to compete.

At 44, a new-look Serena is making a surprise comeback to the top level of professional tennis

The superstar pair hug on the court after losing their first-round US Open match back in 2022

'I’m especially grateful to tournament director, Jamie Baker, and the entire tournament team for giving me every opportunity to recover. Thank you to the fans for your incredible support and for making this comeback so meaningful…All I can say is stay tuned to a city near you…'

The post was accompanied by a video of the 23-time Grand Slam champion limping along with her right leg heavily bandaged, with her daughter Olympia playing with her walking stick.

There were also pictures of Williams receiving medical treatment, and Serena's post added: 'The photo of the syringes is the fluid they drained from my knee after my singles match - yikes! The good news is that my knee shouldn't swell or collect that much fluid again. The bad news is that, as hard as I tried, I wasn’t able to be ready for doubles.'

There was a very mixed reaction to Serena's decision to pull out, with some sympathetic and others furious that she had taken away other, younger, players' opportunities to compete in the prestigious tournament.

Sports.title: British boxer Raven Chapman, 32, rushed to hospital and put in medically-induced coma after training incident in Denmark - as family start fundraiser to return her to the UK
Sports.content:
British boxer Raven Chapman, 32, rushed to hospital and put in medically-induced coma after training incident in Denmark - as family start fundraiser to return her to the UK

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

British boxer Raven Chapman is recovering after undergoing emergency brain surgery and spending almost two weeks in an induced coma following a serious injury sustained during sparring.

The 32-year-old collapsed after a training session in Denmark on July 24 and was taken by air ambulance to hospital, where doctors diagnosed a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

Chapman underwent emergency surgery to stop the bleeding and reduce swelling before being placed in an induced coma to aid her recovery.

In an update released by her team, doctors have now started reducing her sedation as treatment continues.

Plans are also being made for her to be transferred to a hospital in the UK, where she is expected to begin what is likely to be a lengthy rehabilitation.

A statement from her team said: 'Doctors are doing everything they can to support her recovery, and we remain hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time.

British boxer Raven Chapman is recovering after undergoing emergency brain surgery and spending almost two weeks in an induced coma

The 32-year-old collapsed after a training session in Denmark on July 24 and was taken by air ambulance to hospital, where doctors diagnosed a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema

The GoFundMe Link can be accessed here.

'Raven's family are in Denmark supporting her during this incredibly difficult time. We kindly ask that their privacy is respected.

'At this stage, this is the only update we are able to provide. If there are any significant developments, we will share further information when it is appropriate to do so.

'Thank you for your continued support. Please keep Raven and her loved ones in your thoughts during this challenging time.'

A fundraising page has also been launched to help cover the costs of Chapman's rehabilitation and ongoing care. More than £46,000 has already been donated towards a £80,000 target.

Several stars from the boxing world have donated, with the likes of Nakisa Bidarian, Terri Harper, Ellie Scotney and Skye Nicholson among those to have contributed.

Former promoter Frank Warren shared the appeal on social media, writing: 'Raven is fully in my thoughts this morning, I'm really hoping she can pull through and get home safely.

'Everyone at Queensberry is behind you Raven, we're all hoping you can pull through this.'

Queensberry also issued its own statement, saying: 'Everyone at Queensberry is devastated to hear about our former fighter Raven Chapman. We're all hoping for a full recovery.'

Queensberry Promotions also donated £20,000, while Eddie Hearn contributed £5,000.

Chapman, from Norwich, has a professional record of 10 wins and two defeats. She challenged for the WBC featherweight world title in 2024, losing on points to Skye Nicholson in Riyadh.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'offers Morocco World Cup final' in exchange for support
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'offers Morocco World Cup final' in exchange for support

Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal and Gianni Infantino has reportedly offered them the chance to stage the final - on one condition

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's position at FIFA may be coming under threat (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Beleaguered FIFA chief Gianni Infantino has reportedly offered Morocco the chance to host the World Cup final in 2030 in exchange for the nation's support as he desperately tries to cling to power.

‌



Infantino is in Morocco where he has held a crisis meeting of FIFA officials today as calls for him to resign over his botched plot to sell off the World Cup intensify.

‌



The 2023 edition of the tournament will be hosted across Spain, Portugal and Morocco as well as three matches played in South America.

‌



Morocco have been one of Infantino's biggest supporters over the course of his decade in charge of FIFA and were rewarded with co-hosting rights for the World Cup.

Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today READ MORE :

They want to host the final in the new 115,000-seat Hassan II stadium in Casablanca which will be the largest football stadium in the world when it is built.

‌



And, according to The Times, Infantino has promised Morocco they will host the final of the tournament, rather than the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid, if they publicly endorse him in the face of mouting criticism.

But Infantino is said to be concerned over the lack of support from Saudi Arabia who will host the 2034 World Cup.

Former Real Madrid and Barcelona star Luis Figo has become the latest big name to denounce Infantino with many calling for him to resign immediately.

‌



He described Infantino's conduct as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour” he has ever witnessed. “And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game,” he added.

Figo went on: "Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate. He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest of the game he is supposed to serve.

View 2 Images Luis Figo alongside Gianni Infantino in 2024

‌



“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

It comes after legendary former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger, now head of football development at FIFA, distance himself from the doomed plot to sell off the World Cup.

“At FIFA, I am the chief of global football development," Wenger said.

‌



“Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world.

“In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.”

Sports.title: Lord Sebastian Coe hails 'year for the ages' ahead of European Athletics Championships on home soil
Sports.content:
Lord Sebastian Coe hails 'year for the ages' ahead of European Athletics Championships on home soil

Keely Hodgkinson, the Olympic champion over 800m, will be one of the main attractions in the latter event, where GB will be looking to come away with a hatful of medals

View Image Keely Hodgkinson has been praised by Sebastian Coe (Image: Getty)

British athletics is experiencing a 'year for the ages' according to Sebastian Coe.

‌



The president of World Athletics was in London in July to see Josh Kerr break the 27-year-old mile world record – a mark that Lord Coe set three times during his own career – while this summer features a pair of home championships, the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the upcoming European Championships in Birmingham.

‌



Keely Hodgkinson, the Olympic champion over 800m, will be one of the main attractions in the latter event, where GB will be looking to come away with a hatful of medals. And for Lord Coe, there is no question that Britain’s competitiveness on the international scene is in large part down to The National Lottery, launched in 1994.

‌



It has provided nearly £1.8 billion in funding to elite sport in the UK via UKSport in more than 30 years since, a game-changing investment according to Lord Coe.

He said: “It really is a year for the ages for British athletics. We have a European Championships, a Commonwealth Games, a World Under-20 Championships, where we have a very strong British team, and then the Ultimate Championships at the end of the year, which I'm sure will showcase a number of British athletes.

“The point I'd make is that all that is done in large part because of the National Lottery. Let's be absolutely blunt about it. In 1996, two years after The National Lottery was created but with no impact, we had the poorest performance we have had at an Olympic Games, we only had one gold medal (overall), we didn’t have a single gold medal in track and field that year. We were 36th on the medal table.

‌



“You could then suddenly plot the journey: 2000, a big improvement, 2004 another significant improvement, 2008 in Beijing off the graph, I think we finished fourth on the medals table, then London. Then I was chair of the British Olympic Association between 2012 and 2016, and I'm really pleased that I retired on our biggest medal haul in Rio.

“The National Lottery and consistent levels of funding, there is no coincidence, if you have the funding, you will get the performances. It’s been a game changer.”

The impact of The National Lottery is particularly resonant for Lord Coe, who had swapped the track for politics at the time of its introduction. In fact, he was one of the key figures in getting the original bill through parliament.

Article continues below

He added: “I'm very proud of it. It was an interesting journey for me because my first committee role as an MP was to sit on the National Lottery Bill Committee, so I was one of the government members on the committee and it was the arm wrestle around the shareholder agreement.

“It was that committee that delivered the vision that John Major set and I genuinely believe that his legacy of creating The National Lottery and the life-changing elements of that lottery for communities the length and breadth of the country is one of the strongest legacies any peacetime Prime Minister can point to.”

The funding continues to have a huge impact on British sport to this day, and as the continent’s best athletes descend on the Alexander Stadium in Birmingham, its effects will be vital for home athletes looking to impress.

Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah spotted in new shirt for first time as Liverpool icon mobbed after transfer

Mohamed Salah is joining a new club after weeks of speculation over his future having left Liverpool this summer following nine years at the club

View 2 Images Liverpool icon Mohamed Salah has landed in Turkey ahead of a move to Trabzonspor (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah has arrived in Istanbul wearing Trabzonspor's shirt, having agreed to join the Turkish side after leaving Liverpool at the end of last season. The 34-year-old will pen a two-year deal, according to reports.

‌



The Egyptian had been heavily linked with a move to Saudi Arabia but clubs in Turkey also pushed hard for his signature. Talks with Besiktas over a transfer took place last month, only for the move to break down.

‌



But it's now Trabzonspor who have won the race for his signature, with the club announcing they were in transfer talks with Salah on Tuesday night and that he would arrive in Trabzon on Wednesday.

‌

They stated: "Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5. The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

"The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club’s official communication channels during the day."

Salah was greeted by several journalists outside of the airport as well as fans.

‌



Salah will link up with Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, who has returned to the club on loan for a second season. Former Manchester City defender Stefan Savic is another ex‑Premier League player currently plying his trade with the Super Lig side.

Salah bid an emotional farewell when his plan to exit the Reds was announced in March. ""Liverpool is not just a football club, it's a passion, it's a history, it's a spirit," he said. "I can't explain in words to anyone not part of this club.

Sports.title: How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer
Sports.content:
How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer

Arsenal are closing on their first major signing of the summer in Bruno Guimaraes whilst they're tracking Vinicius Junior's situation as the Premier League champions seek to add more quality

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to swap Newcastle for Arsenal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle as they look to land their biggest coup of the summer so far.

‌



The Premier League champions are already favourites to defend their title and have gone after proven talent with the Brazilian set to move for £75million. It became clear weeks ago that Guimaraes wanted out of St James' Park and had cited Arsenal as his ideal destination.

‌



Bolstering midfield was not necessarily a priority at the Emirates, but when a player of his quality became available a swoop was always on the cards. Declan Rice is the only guaranteed starter in the Arsenal midfield, leaving Mikel Arteta to fit pieces of the jigsaw around him.

‌



Guimaraes has been the driving force behind Newcastle's rise - and the club were linked with him when he moved to England from Lyon back in 2022.

The 29-year-old will battle with the likes of Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi for a starting role, whilst Arsenal could equally look to play with a flat three, as opposed to two sitting and one playmaker. Zubimendi and Guimaraes have shown themselves more than capable of picking passes between the lines and stretching defences.

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

One man who may well suffer a knock-on effect should Guimaraes head south is Martin Odegaard. Once the team's unchallenged playmaker, the Norwegian has seen more and more individuals join who can challenge him for his spot. He was injured for periods last term but he may not enjoy the untouchable status he once did.

‌



Arsenal, in the wake of their Champions League final loss, where they were dominated from a footballing point of view, were urged to add more quality in the final third.

They could yet bring in one of the world's best as they continue to track Vinicius Junior's situation at Real Madrid. The winger is about to enter the final year of his contract at the Bernabeu and Los Blancos want to avoid losing him for nothing.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is locked in a contract standoff with Real Madrid (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Their negotiations centre on the player's image rights and where he sits in the financial pecking order. Vinicius wants to earn the same as Kylian Mbappe, Real's top earner, but the club are reluctant to do so - and Arsenal could yet swoop in as reports claim they would make him the Premier League's highest-ever earner.

That would see him pocket weekly wages that are north of £500,000-a-week. Such an investment would see Vinicius go straight in on Arsenal's left side with Bukayo Saka still the team's main man on the right, even if his form has dropped off over the last 12 months.

The central figure of their attack remains an issue, despite the £64m investment they made in Viktor Gyokeres last summer. The Swede scored 20 times in his debut season but question marks remain and he was ultimately left out for the Champions League final against PSG.

‌



Kai Havertz, who scored that night in Budapest, was picked instead and whilst the German links play better than anyone in the Arsenal side, his lack of goals have been cited as an issue when compared to some of Europe's heavyweights. It leaves Arteta with a decision on who to back - or whether to dip back into the market.

View 3 Images Arsenal would likely have to shell out £200m in order to land Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jnr

Arsenal's frontline is already heavily congested with Noni Madueke, Gabriel Martinelli, Eberechi Eze, new signing Christos Tzolis and academy graduate Ethan Nwaneri all eyeing minutes. The latter was forced to head out on loan last term after being continually overlooked.

‌



Defensively Arsenal remain one of Europe's best - if not the best. Their world class centre-half pairing of Gabriel and William Saliba has been the cornerstone of their rise in recent years, although the Frenchman will spend a period on the sidelines, leaving someone to fill the void initially.

Piero Hincapie was signed permanently this summer and has impressed at left-back whilst Jurrien Timber, when fit, is perhaps the most versatile defender in the team and equally impressive at centre-half or on either flank.

David Raya, off the back of having to accept not being Spain's No 1, continues to prove himself as one of the world's best for Arsenal. The club have signed Illan Meslier to serve as a back-up option.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr is a game-changing transfer that even non-Arsenal fans should want done
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr is a game-changing transfer that even non-Arsenal fans should want done

Arsenal have managed to tempt Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle and the Premier League champions are still hopeful of bringing Real Madrid's star attacker to the Premier League

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior is having make-or-break contract talks with Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is a solid, high-end signing for Arsenal but it is not a game-changing transfer. At Newcastle United, the Brazilian has proven himself to be a very effective performer in the context of the Premier League’s particular demands.

‌



For a start, he covers a lot of ground. In a 4-3 win over Leeds United at St James’ Park in January of this year, Guimaraes ran 13.24km - that is well over eight miles. Only two other players broke the 13km mark in a single Premier League game last season. Manchester City’s Bernardo Silva did it against Nottingham Forest and Brighton’s Pascal Gross did it twice, against City and Chelsea.

‌



Guimaraes is a committed character, that is for sure. It is probably fair to say he was the heartbeat of the Eddie Howe team that ended Newcastle’s long wait for a major trophy and qualified for two Champions League campaigns.

‌



In those Champions League campaigns, Guimaraes featured in 13 matches, failed to score and produced only one assist. His Premier League numbers are significantly better, scoring 30 times (two of which were penalties) for Newcastle and contributing 26 assists.

More detailed statistics show Guimaraes has, across the last three seasons, won more duels (697) than any other Premier League player. Mikel Arteta, in common with most Premier League managers, loves a player who can win a duel.

And judging by the prices in most top-level midfield transactions this summer, a fee in the region of £75million for the 28-year-old is a relatively reasonable figure. But he is not a game-changer. His countryman Vinicius Junior most certainly is.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes will soon complete his £75million to Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Vinicius Junior and his advisers are scheduled to meet with Real Madrid executives any time now for what are being seen as make-or-break talks over his contract impasse. The 26-year-old attacker has a year left on his deal and wants a £10million-a-year increase to his current salary of £15million.

Real’s offer stands at an annual £19mllion - still £6million shy. Arsenal would have to shatter any sort of pay-scale they have but this would be a one-off move.

‌



This would be a statement signing of the highest order. For all the Premier League’s self-proclamation about being the best club competition in the world, it still struggles to attract the ultimate marquee players.

They normally go to Real Madrid, not leave Real Madrid. Vinicius Junior has been a flagship player at the Bernabeu and, most significantly, a proven Champions League performer.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr would give Mikel Arteta that extra attacking dimension he needs (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal and Arteta deserved great credit for going all the way to the final - and to a penalty shootout - last season but they lacked just one extra, attacking dimension. Vinicius Junior would provide that.

He has 26 goals and 21 assists in his last 46 Champions League appearances. And while Arsenal fans will rightfully dismiss it as unimportant, Vinicius Junior will make them more watchable. He will make the Premier League more watchable.

Clearly, there is still a lot of work to be done if Arsenal are to tempt Vinicius Junior to the Emirates. But even you are not a Gunner, it is a move that the Premier League should be desperate for.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan

Arsenal have agreed a deal with Newcastle United for Bruno Guimaraes and have their eyes set on their next summer signing

View 2 Images Arsenal are closing in on Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal have reportedly set their sights on a new central defender this summer as they look for cover after William Saliba aggravated a back injury on international duty at the World Cup. The Gunners are closing in on the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes and are exploring a blockbuster deal for Vinicius Junior, but a new defender is also being targeted.

‌



Saliba was replaced in France's semi-final defeat to Spain after going down injured, with new Chelsea signing Mazence Lacroix brought on as his replacement.

‌



Head coach Didier Deschamps did not risk Saliba during the third-placed play-off against England, though he did name the Arsenal defender on the substitutes' bench. Arsenal released a medical update four days later following Saliba's return to London from the United States.

‌



The club confirmed he is expected to miss part of the new season and will be sidelined for a prolonged spell as he undertakes a managed recovery programme. Now, according toFabrizio Romano, the Gunners will bring in a new defender to cover for Saliba.

Alan Brazil gives health update as radio legend returns to air after life-saving operation READ MORE :

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Deschamps revealed ahead of France's final game that Saliba had been managing the injury since March. He said: "William Saliba got injured, and it's problematic. He went through some examinations, and the injury did not worsen. He has faced that injury since March; he had some pain, and unfortunately, the pain was not bearable".

‌



Arsenal, however, maintain that thorough assessments have determined that surgery is not required. Specialist evaluations established that the injury would necessitate a period of rehabilitation instead.

Back troubles previously affected Saliba three years ago. His 2022/23 season was brought to an end prematurely after injuring his back during the second leg of Arsenal's Europa League last-16 encounter against Sporting.

He was sidelined for the final 11 Premier League matches and missed four of France's European Championship qualifiers as well. Saliba made his comeback four months afterwards during Arsenal's pre-season programme.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta will be without William Saliba for the start of the new season (Image: ANTONIN THUILLIER, AFP via Getty Images)

The club have brought in defenders Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber, Piero Hincapie and Riccardo Calafiori since that period, but may have to bring in further defensive reinforcements. This summer, the former has featured as a right-sided centre half, partnering Gabriel against Girona, with boss Mikel Arteta evidently grooming him to deputise for Saliba.

Ben White represents another alternative who can shift infield from right-back to operate centrally. Arsenal, though, continue to monitor the market for cover.

‌



England international Ezri Konsa was said to be under consideration, but Aston Villa's asking price in excess of £50m hampers any prospective transfer. Former Man City defender John Stones was also considered before joining Inter on a free transfer, while Arsenal have also been linked with other defenders.

Arsenal are on the brink of landing a statement signing regarding Guimaraes, after agreeing a £75m deal with Newcastle United for their captain.

The Gunners are also hopeful of pulling off one of the transfers of the summer by signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, who is in the final 12 months of his contract at the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
