World.title: Cabinet Secretary, Home Secretary get one-year extension in service
World.content:
Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan and Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan’s tenures have been extended for another year, according to a government order issued on Wednesday (August 5, 2026).

Mr. Mohan, a 1989 batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Sikkim cadre, was appointed Home Secretary in 2024 and assumed office on August 23, 2024. He was serving as Culture Secretary before his present assignment. A Home Secretary’s tenure is typically for two years.

“The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has approved extension in the service of Govind Mohan, IAS (SK:89) as Home Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs for a period of one year beyond 22.08.2026, that is up to 22.8.2027, in relaxation of the provisions of Fundamental Rule (FR) 56 (d) and Rule 16 (1A) of the All India Services (Death-cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958,” the order said.

The ACC, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the extension in service of Mr. Somanathan as Cabinet Secretary for a further period of one year beyond August 30, 2026, an order issued by the Personnel Ministry said.

Mr. Somanathan, a 1987-batch Indian Administrative Service officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre, was appointed to the post for two years in August 2024.

World.title: After a long delay, portfolios allocated in NDA Cabinet in Puducherry
World.content:
After a protracted delay, portfolios of Ministers in the Cabinet headed by Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy have been announced on Wednesday.

As per government notification, Mr. Rangasamy will handle Confidential and Cabinet Department, Planning and Finance, Revenue and Excise, Personnel and Administrative Reforms, Health and Family Welfare, Local Administration, Transport, Town and Country Planning, Information and Publicity, Urban Basic Services, General Administration, Waqf Board, Science, Technology and Environment, Cooperation and other subjects which are not allocated to other Ministers.

BJP Minister in the NDA Cabinet A. Nammassivayam will handle Home, besides dealing with subjects such as Animal Husbandry, Electricity, Education including Collegiate Education, Forest and Wild Life and Law. The other BJP Minister in the Cabinet, G.N.S. Rajasekaran, will look after portfolios, such as Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Sports and Youth Affairs, DRDA, Community Development, Rural Development and Sainik Welfare.

The AINRC Minister Malladi Krishna Rao will handle Public Works, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Fisheries and Fishermen Welfare, Port, Industries and Commerce and Labour and Employment. Minister P. Rajavelu, who also represents the AINRC, will look after Adi Dravidar Welfare, Art and Culture, Housing, Information Technology, Economics and Statistics and Stationary and Printing.

Another AINRC Minister in the Cabinet V. P. Sivakolundhu has been given the subjects of Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, Social Welfare, Backward Class Welfare, Women and Child Development and Minority Affairs.

The NDA government had faced severe criticism for the delay in providing a functional Cabinet though the Assembly election results were announced on May 4. After the results were declared, Mr. Rangasamy and two other Ministers (one from AINRC and one from BJP) were sworn-in on May 13. A month later, three more Ministers (two from AINRC and one from BJP) were sworn-in on June 17. However, the distribution of portfolios among the Cabinet members was delayed.

World.title: UDF facilitating Sangh agenda in universities, says Pinarayi
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Wednesday alleged that the United Democratic Front (UDF) government was facilitating the Sangh Parivar’s agenda in Kerala’s higher education sector by remaining silent on the Governor’s interventions in universities and abandoning the resistance mounted by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government.

Addressing a public meeting organised in connection with the diamond jubilee of the Kerala University Employees Union here, Mr. Vijayan accused the UDF government of allowing the “saffronisation” of universities by failing to challenge decisions taken through the Chancellor’s office and by endorsing appointments that purportedly advanced the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) agenda.

Defending the previous LDF government’s handling of university affairs, Mr. Vijayan said it had repeatedly approached the Kerala High Court and the Supreme Court over issues relating to the appointment of Vice-Chancellors in universities, including the APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University and the Digital University Kerala.

As a result, the LDF government had then secured favourable judgments in most of the cases. He pointed out that the the apex court had held that the panel for appointing temporary V-Cs should be submitted to the Chief Minister and that the Governor should make appointments according to the order of preference recommended by the Chief Minister. Although the Governor later sought a review of the judgment, the Supreme Court declined to modify its original order, he added.

The LDF government had also legally challenged the Governor’s nomination of “Sangh Parivar sympathisers” to the governing bodies of universities. “The Congress had then defended the Governor’s actions. Notably, the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president also justified the inclusion of Sangh Parivar supporters, while accepting the Senate nominations offered by the Governor,” he alleged.

Mr. Vijayan said the present UDF government had effectively ended the resistance against attempts to “saffronise” universities and was displaying an eagerness to compromise the secular foundations of Kerala’s higher education system.

He cited the appointment of a purported leader of a Sangh Parivar-affiliated teachers’ organisation as V-C of Mahatma Gandhi University and the subsequent induction of 19 RSS sympathisers into the university Senate as examples of the alleged shift. The UDF government, he said, had not questioned either development and had instead adopted a supportive stance.

The Leader of the Opposition also questioned the Governor’s decision to convene meetings of government officials in connection with the observance of International Yoga Day on university campuses. Such meetings were unconstitutional and beyond the Governor’s authority, he alleged.

“Instead of questioning the Governor’s actions, the government bent its spine and remained silent,” he said.

He also accused the Centre of attempting to dismantle the very concept of public universities and also undermining the powers of States in higher education through its ‘One Nation, One Entrance Examination’ policy and centralised admission mechanisms.

Union president Santhosh G. Nair and general secretary A. Sajith Khan also spoke on the occasion.

World.title: Palani land case: HC dismisses advance bail plea of suspended Sub-Registrar
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday dismissed the anticipatory bail petition filed by suspended Sub-Registrar Justin Manikandan Subramanian, one of the accused in the Palani math land sale case.

Justice K. Rajasekar cancelled the interim bail granted to him, and also dismissed the anticipatory bail petition filed by another accused, Jeyaprakash.

The court said the case under investigation by the CB-CID revealed that accused Anwardeen was actively involved in fabrication of records and was taking several steps to grab the property from 1998 onwards.

Anwardeen who had been arrested in the case disclosed various facts regarding the manner in which the sale deed came to be registered and the various acts done by the accused to force the Registration Department to conclude the registration.

It is said that Jeyaprakash, an associate of Anwardeen, was directed to influence the then Sub Registrar Balasundar. Since Balasundar did not accept their illegal acts, they mounted pressure on him, and obtained a court order to register the sale deed.

Due to the pressure mounted on him, Mr. Balasundar went on leave, after completing the initial registration process. He made an entry in the minutes book that the registration of the document had been objected to by the temple and the temple had filed a writ appeal.

The State submitted that there was concentrated telephonic communication between the petitioners, Sub-Registrar Justin Manikandan Subramanian, who registered the document, and document writer Jeyaprakash before and during the registration of the document.

Without considering the minutes and remarks recorded by the then Sub-Registrar, Justin Manikandan Subramanian completed the registration process by assigning the document number, which clearly revealed that he had not acted bonafidely, and acted intentionally to benefit the other accused.

During the course of the arguments, Jeyaprakash submitted that he was not a document writer.

The court said granting anticipatory bail to the petitioners at this stage would hamper the investigation. Earlier, the court dismissed the anticipatory bail petition of one of the accused, K. Vellathurai.

The State submitted a status report on the progress made in the investigation in the case to a Division Bench of Justices C.V. Karthikeyan and R. Sakthivel. The court posted petitions seeking a CBI probe for hearing to August 12.

Meanwhile, Judicial Magistrate I, Dindigul, S. Packiaraj, granted the CB-CID till Friday the custody of the four arrested accused — D. Murugadass, who sold the land; K. Vellathurai and D. Sethupathi, both buyers of the land; and S. Anwardeen, who reportedly facilitated the deal.

World.title: Kerala rain 2026: Rain eases in Thrissur, relief camps continue
World.content:
Monsoon rain has eased across Thrissur district, but the administration remains on alert as controlled water is being released from the Poringalkuthu dam, prompting a warning for residents along the Chalakudy river, and fresh evacuations have been ordered in a landslip-prone area near the Puthur Zoological Park. As of now, 59 people continue to stay in relief camps in the district.

According to the district administration, five relief camps were functioning across the district as of 12 noon on Wednesday, accommodating 19 families. The residents include 30 men, 20 women and nine children, including 18 senior citizens. The relief camp at Nellayi JUPS has been closed.

Three camps are operating in Mukundapuram taluk, sheltering five families with 15 people. Two camps are functioning in Thrissur taluk, housing 14 families and 44 people, with the Government Polytechnic camp at Nedupuzha accounting for the largest number of evacuees.

The district administration has also issued a caution for people living along the banks of the Chalakudy river after the water level in the Poringalkuthu dam touched its crest level of 419.40 m. The dam’s crest gates have been kept open to regulate the reservoir level, resulting in additional discharge into the river. Residents in low-lying areas along the river have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid entering the river or flood-prone areas.

Meanwhile, the administration has ordered the evacuation of three families from the Anakkuzhi-Thonippara area at Kainoor, near the Puthur Zoological Park, following an increased threat of landslips.

The decision was taken after District Collector Shikha Surendran and K. Rajan, MLA, visited the site. The functioning of a nearby anganwadi has also been suspended temporarily as a precaution.

Concern intensified after three large trees were uprooted with a loud rumble from the hilltop overlooking the settlement on Tuesday night, raising fears of a possible landslip. Officials said the evacuation was ordered to eliminate the risk to human life while the area is monitored for further ground movement.

World.title: Include CBSE-sector representatives on panels for readying education policies: council
World.content:
The Council of CBSE Schools Kerala (CCSK) has urged Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to include representatives from the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) sector in committees constituted for formulating education policies and taking key decisions concerning the unaided school sector.

The council recommended the establishment of a permanent coordination and communication mechanism between the State’s General Education department and CBSE schools.

The recommendations were submitted as part of the council’s activity report presented to the Chief Minister.

For collaboration

The council underscored that effective collaboration between the government and private educational institutions was essential to ensure quality education for all students, irrespective of differences in Central and State curricula.

It mooted strengthening safety measures in schools and implementing coordinated initiatives to ensure the physical, mental, and the social well-being of students.

The council requested the government to take urgent steps to ensure the continuation of the Kerala State Schools Sports Meet, which has been organised for the past five years by the Kerala State Sports Council in association with the CCSK, bringing together students from CBSE, ICSE, Kendriya Vidyalayas, and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas across the State.

Support for Operation Toofan

Reiterating its commitment to student welfare, the council extended its full support to the State government’s ‘Operation Toofan’ anti-drug and anti-tobacco campaign. The council announced that awareness programmes involving students, teachers, and parents would be further strengthened in CBSE schools throughout Kerala.

The memorandum, also submitted to Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen and Minister for Sports O.J. Janeesh, outlined a wide range of educational, social, cultural, artistic, sports, and student empowerment initiatives undertaken by CCSK across the State.

The Chief Minister and the Ministers concerned assured the council that the recommendations would be given serious consideration, a statement on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) said.

The delegation comprised Indira Rajan, secretary general, National Council of CBSE Schools; Suchithra Shaijinth, general secretary, Council of CBSE Schools Kerala; and Fr. Johny Kanjirathinkal, zonal president.

World.title: RBI has funds to pay for UPI platform without having to charge merchants, customers
World.content:
Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) said that “someone will have to pay the cost” of UPI transactions, which are currently free for merchants and customers. The cost is currently being borne by banks and the National Payment Corporation of India.

Mr. Malhotra was responding to media queries in the context of recent moves by the government to pave the way for a charge to be levied on such transactions. If implemented, certain merchants would have to pay banks for the use of the UPI platform, which experts say they would pass on to customers.

An analysis by The Hindu has found that the RBI itself has more than enough funds to pay for the UPI platform’s use, without involving any additional charge on merchants or customers. This additional cost would amount to between 3-8.5% of what the central bank transferred to the Union government as its annual surplus.

Further, even with the volume of UPI transactions growing 425% over the last five years, the quantum of surpluses transferred by the RBI to the Union government has grown at more than double that rate.

Provisions to make ‘someone’ pay

“The costs have to be paid by someone,” Mr. Malhotra said. “We all want that this public infrastructure should continue to strengthen. Let’s wait and watch for further developments on this.

“The cost is already getting passed on,” he added. “It may not be directly on to the very user, but someone is paying the cost. This is what I meant when I said someone will have to pay the cost. What is important is that we continue to invest and we continue to find the means, whether it is MDR or other things.”

A provision in the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 introduced in Parliament by the government on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) dilutes the earlier restrictions imposed on banks from imposing charges such as a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions. Instead, it says that the government can notify the kinds of transactions that can attract such a charge.

Cost of running UPI

According to sources in the government, the proposal to allow banks to levy an MDR is currently limited to a small sub-set of merchants — those with an annual turnover of Rs 1-1.5 crore — and to transactions above ₹2,000 in value.

However, the wording of the Bill provides an avenue for this charge to be levied on a wider set of transactions in the future.

According to banking industry officials, the UPI platform currently costs about ₹0.4-1 per transaction to operate and maintain. Official data shows that 24,161.69 crore UPI transactions were conducted in 2025-26. This would peg the cost of running the platform at ₹9,664 to ₹24,161 crore per year.

Surplus available

The RBI earned approximately ₹4.3 lakh crore in 2025-26. Out of this, it transferred about ₹2.9 lakh crore to the Union government as surplus for 2025-26. The cost of running the UPI platform that year would have worked out to 3-8.5% of this amount.

RBI surplus transfers have grown from ₹30,307.45 crore in 2021-22 to about ₹2.9 lakh crore in 2025-26, a growth of 857%. Over this period, the volume of UPI transactions grew 425%.

This shows that, even with this rapid growth in UPI adoption, the RBI surpluses have grown more than enough to cover the cost of all UPI transactions.

World.title: Pakistan, Iran agree to keep border crossings open round the clock to boost trade
World.content:
Pakistan and Iran on Wednesday agreed to further expand trade ties by keeping border crossings open round the clock, improving logistics and harmonising customs procedures.

The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and a six-member Iranian delegation, led by Iran’s Minister for Industry, Mine and Trade Mohammad Atabak, in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

During the meeting, the prime minister said that Pakistan highly valued its relations with its close, brotherly neighbour Iran, the PMO said.

“Pakistan will continue its sincere efforts for peace in the region,” PM Shehbaz was quoted as saying.

He added that he had recently held a productive discussion with Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian on establishing lasting peace in the region and further enhancing Pakistan-Iran bilateral relations, particularly in trade, the statement said.

During the meeting, the prime minister expressed hope that sustained efforts would enable both countries to achieve the bilateral trade target of $10 billion set by their leadership, it added.

“Both countries will benefit from increased trade, particularly in food, agricultural commodities and related products,” PM Shehbaz said.

According to the statement, the meeting also agreed to promote border trade between Pakistan and Iran by expanding facilities to keep border crossings open 24 hours a day.

“Both sides also agreed to enhance cooperation in the mining sector, particularly in the processing and value addition of precious stones,” it stated.

The Iranian minister said he was grateful to Pakistan for the warm welcome and excellent hospitality.

He praised the Pakistani leadership and people for their “sincere diplomatic efforts for regional peace and their expression of solidarity with Iran,” the statement said.

“Iran is keen to further expand its economic and trade relations with Pakistan,” Atabak was quoted as saying.

“Technical-level negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between Pakistan and Iran are currently underway,” he added.

On Tuesday, both countries also reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion.

In April, Pakistan’s commerce ministry had notified six transit routes for the transportation of goods to Iran via Pakistani sea ports in Gwadar and Karachi. The development had come amid reports that thousands of containers destined for Iran are awaiting clearance at Pakistani ports.

Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict in the Middle East that has strained economies in the region and beyond.

World.title: Search team reaches Broad Peak base camp with body of renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja
World.content:
A search team has transported the bodies of renowned climber Nirmal Purja and three of his team members to the base camp of the mountain where they were killed in an avalanche, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Wednesday.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by 43-year-old British-Nepali climber Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. His company confirmed there were no survivors.

“On behalf of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, it is announced with great sadness to confirm that, following an exceptionally challenging and technically demanding recovery operation on Broad Peak, the bodies of Nirmal Purja, Zhong Wang, Nima Sherpa, and Kilu Sherpa have been successfully recovered and have now arrived safely at Base Camp,” the ACP posted on social media, referring to a Chinese mountaineer and two other Nepali climbers.

“While today marks an important milestone, three climbers remain missing,” the club said.

“We remain committed to supporting all possible efforts to locate and recover them, whenever conditions allow, so that they too may be returned home to their loved ones,” it added.

The remains of three other members of the team — an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man — had already been flown off the mountain to Skardu.

The bodies of Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi of Hunza and two Nepali nationals have not yet been recovered. Funeral prayers were offered in absentia for Sakhi in his hometown of Aliabad in Hunza on Monday, where hundreds of people paid tribute to the young mountaineer and offered condolences to his family.

Shock and grief have hit members of the alpine climbing community with the President of Nepal’s National Mountain Guide Association Tul Singh Gurung saying they had “lost a generation of accomplished mountaineers”.

The ACP said the recovered bodies of the four climbers would be returned to their families.

The club’s president, Major General (retd.) Irfan Arshad Khan, told Dawn that the deceased climbers would be airlifted to Skardu by helicopters, which had been unable to operate for the last three days due to adverse weather conditions.

“We hope this recovery brings them a measure of peace and the opportunity to lay their loved ones to rest with the dignity they deserve,” the club said.

It extended its gratitude to those leading and supporting rescue efforts — including the ground recovery team led by Mingma G and supported by Sirbaz Khan — as well as the dedicated Pakistani and Nepali recovery teams, the Pakistan Army, the governments of Pakistan and Gilgit-Baltistan, local authorities, the British High Commission, and the Embassy of Nepal for their invaluable support throughout the mission.

Nirmal’s business partner and Member of Nepal’s House of Representatives Mingma David Sherpa, who is currently monitoring the rescue and search operation, appreciated the “courage, professionalism, and selfless commitment” of the ground recovery team, saying, “We are deeply grateful to every member of the team for carrying out this mission under extremely difficult and dangerous conditions.”

“Our thoughts also remain with the families of the three climbers who are still missing. We remain committed to supporting every possible effort to bring them home when conditions safely allow,” he added.

Broad Peak is the world’s 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents.

It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.

World.title: ‘No sovereignty over East Jerusalem’: Dar condemns Al-Aqsa incursions by ‘extremist Israeli settlers’
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said that Israel has no sovereignty over East Jerusalem and its holy sites, condemning the incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque by “extremist Israeli settlers”.

Addressing the ministerial conference in Amman, Jordan, he said that the illegal actions of Israel — the occupying power in occupied Palestine — continued to threaten the sanctity and historical character of the holy sites in Jerusalem.

“They undermine international law, disregard UN resolutions, and further erode the prospect of a just, comprehensive and lasting peace.”

“Pakistan condemns in the strongest possible terms the continued incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque by extremist Israeli settlers encouraged by senior Israeli ministers and carried out under the protection of occupying forces,” FM Dar stated.

By deliberately undermining the religious and historical status of Jerusalem, FM Dar emphasised that Israel was provoking the sentiments of billions of Muslims across the globe.

“This appears not only an attempt to undermine regional peace, security and stability but also to drag followers of various religions into a wider conflict,” he said, adding, “We cannot and must not allow that.”

“Pakistan condemns Israeli actions and provocations in the strongest possible terms,” he said.

He stressed that there should be no ambiguity that Israel has no sovereignty over occupied East Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

“All measures seeking to alter its character and status are null and void and without any legal effect,” he added.

The foreign minister said Pakistan reaffirmed its support for the historic and special role played by Jordan and recognised the Jerusalem Endowment and Al-Aqsa Affairs Department, affiliated with the Jordanian Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs, as the legal authority with exclusive jurisdiction over the administration of Al-Aqsa Mosque.

Moreover, FM Dar said that Pakistan also remained “deeply concerned” over the continuous expansion of illegal Israeli settlements, the establishment of new settlements and the continued oppression of the Palestinian people.

“These policies violate international law and further entrench an unlawful occupation.”

In Gaza, he said that the humanitarian situation was extremely fragile.

“The ceasefire and the implementation of the elements of the Gaza Peace Plan have yielded some improvements; however, 59pc of the population still faces food insecurity and health crises,” FM Dar said.

Since the ceasefire, he said that over 1,100 Palestinians had been killed, which called into question the full and faithful implementation of the Gaza Peace Plan.

“Arab and Islamic countries must act with unity, resolve and collective action and should first reaffirm the protection of Jerusalem and the holy sites, demanding an immediate cessation of all violations against Al-Aqsa Mosque, preservation of the historical and legal status quo, and unrestricted access to the Old City of Jerusalem and the holy sites,” he said.

He said that Arab and Islamic countries should also reject “illegal Israeli settlement activities, annexation attempts, forced displacements, and demographic changes in the occupied Palestinian territory”.

“We should support the full and faithful implementation of the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict and UNSC Resolution No. 2803,” the foreign minister said, adding, “We should also strengthen Arab and Islamic coordination and diplomatic efforts to ensure the protection of the Kashmiri people.”

Meetings on sidelines

FM Dar also held one-on-one meetings with the foreign ministers of Turkiye, Algeria and Egypt on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, the FO said.

In his meeting with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, FM Dar “exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual interest,” it said.

During his meeting with Egyptian Foreign Minister Dr Badr Abdelatty, Dar discussed Pakistan-Egypt relations, regional and international developments, and exchanged views on matters of mutual interest, the FO said.

Meanwhile, in his meeting with Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmad Attaf, FM Dar “discussed Pakistan-Algeria bilateral relations and explored ways to enhance cooperation in trade, investment, information technology, agriculture and other areas of mutual interest”.

Moreover, the foreign ministers of the R-4 Group, comprising Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, also met in Amman on the sidelines of the ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, the FO said.

“The ministers reiterated their unwavering support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state on the basis of the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions,” it added.

According to the FO, the R-4 Group’s foreign ministers reaffirmed that a “just, comprehensive and lasting settlement” of the Palestinian issue remained indispensable to achieving enduring peace and stability in the Middle East.

The ministers also reviewed the evolving regional situation and reaffirmed the importance of continued consultation and close coordination among the four countries in advancing regional stability, emphasising that dialogue and diplomacy remained essential to fostering stability and preventing further escalation in the region, the FO stated.

DPM meets Jordanian counterpart

Dar met his Jordanian counterpart, with the “deteriorating situation in the occupied West Bank” coming under discussion, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The FO said Dar met Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ayman Safadi on the sidelines of a Ministerial Meeting in Amman to discuss the situation in occupied Jerusalem.

The FO said that the foreign ministers exchanged views on regional developments, in particular on the deteriorating situation in the occupied West Bank. Dar appreciated Jordan’s role in safeguarding the Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem and its support for the Palestinian people, it added.

“The two leaders welcomed the growing momentum in Pakistan–Jordan bilateral relations and reaffirmed [their commitment] to further enhancing cooperation across political, defence, economic, educational, cultural and people-to-people domains,” it added.

Dar and Safadi also discussed the situation in the region, including the recent developments in the conflict between the United States and Iran.

They underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for de-escalation and reaffirmed their close coordination at bilateral and multilateral levels to promote peace and stability, including at the United Nations and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the statement added.

Separately, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Abdisalam Abdi Ali, the Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Somalia. Alongside exchanging views on regional developments, the foreign ministers also reviewed the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries.

According to the FO, they discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in the “political, economic, defence, education, and capacity-building sectors”. They also reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination at multilateral forums, it added.

According to the FO, Dar is in Jordan to attend a ministerial meeting aimed at formulating a unified position on the situation in occupied Jerusalem.

It said that he would “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Palestinian people and their just cause” at the ministerial meeting bringing together foreign ministers from Arab League member states and a group of Islamic countries to discuss the deteriorating situation in occupied Jerusalem.

The foreign minister is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts on the sidelines of the meeting to exchange views on regional developments including Palestine.

The FO termed Dar’s participation in the ministerial meeting “a manifestation of Pakistan’s principled support for the Palestinian people” and its commitment to the establishment of an “independent, sovereign and contiguous” State of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

Pakistan and other Muslim countries have repeatedly condemned “continued incursions by extremist Israeli settlers” into Al Aqsa Mosque — Islam’s third-holiest site, located in east Jerusalem, which Israel captured in 1967 and later annexed.

The Al-Aqsa compound is a central symbol of Palestinian identity and also a frequent flashpoint. Under long-standing arrangements, Jewish people may visit the compound, but are not permitted to pray there. While Israel says it is committed to maintaining this status quo, Palestinians fear it is being eroded.

The foreign ministers of Pakistan and eight other Muslim countries in June expressed their “categorical rejection” of any attempts to alter the historical and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites.

World.title: Roads blocked, traffic disrupted as PTI holds rally near Karachi Press Club
World.content:
KARACHI: The PTI held a protest near the Karachi Press Club (KPC) on Wednesday to mark three years since the imprisonment of party founder Imran Khan and demand his release.

The demonstration led to traffic disruptions in the surrounding areas after authorities blocked routes leading to the venue, causing severe congestion and leaving commuters stranded for extended periods.

A screenshot showing closed roads in Karachi’s Saddar Town area. — Screengrab from Google Maps

A police official, who wished not to be named, said that some PTI workers and leaders were detained near the Press Club.

They confirmed that police resorted to tear gas shelling and used baton charges to disperse the demonstrators, adding that after the police action, the road was cleared for traffic in the evening.

The PTI in a statement said it staged demonstrations in Karachi, Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Nawabshah, Umerkot, Mithi and other parts of Sindh, with participants demanding Imran’s release.

In Karachi, the demonstration was led by PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh, Karachi President Raja Azhar, PTI Sindh General Secretary Dr Masroor Sial and Karachi General Secretary Arsalan Khalid. They and other party leaders led workers towards the Karachi Press Club, according to the statement.

“However, according to the party, police blocked all routes leading to the Press Club by placing containers and completely sealed the area to stop protesters from reaching the venue,” the statement claimed.

“PTI workers later held a peaceful demonstration near Zaibunnisa Street and Fawara Chowk in Saddar. The party alleged that police resorted to tear gas shelling and baton charge against peaceful protesters, leaving several workers injured,” it alleged.

PTI demonstrators stage a protest in Karachi’s Saddar Town area on August 5, 2026. — Photo courtesy PTI

The PTI alleged that the police arrested more than ten workers in the metropolis, including Sial. The party further claimed that six PTI workers were arrested in Pano Aqil and fifteen workers in Kandhkot, with cases also registered against them.

Addressing the protesters, Sheikh demanded the immediate release of Dr Masroor Sial and all detained workers in Karachi, Pano Aqil and Kandhkot, while Raza Azhar said the PTI “formally submitted an application seeking permission for the peaceful protest, yet police still resorted to unlawful use of force”.

Sheikh also took to X and claimed that the route to the KPC had been blocked by containers, slamming the PPP government for sealing off the area.

“The Karachi Press Club is neither a Red Zone nor a sensitive security area, yet the PPP government has blocked public access and trampled the constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” he wrote.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the congestion and issued strict instructions to the Sindh inspector general and the Karachi additional inspector general to restore traffic flow.

“Traffic should be cleared from Sadar, Old City Area, MA Jinnah Road and Zainab Market immediately,” he was quoted as saying in a statement from his office. “Additional traffic police personnel should be deployed on the roads and a report should be submitted.”

He further ordered that queues of cars on Napier Road, Regal Chowk and Bolton Market should also be cleared.

Similarly, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar sought details from the Karachi Traffic deputy inspector general (DIG) on the traffic jams in the city, with a statement from his office saying that the cause behind the disruption should be determined.

“District police should help traffic police in clearing the roads and highways,” Lanjar was quoted as saying. “The difficulties faced by citizens should be immediately addressed.”

He ordered that traffic police personnel should be stationed on all major arteries and pressure points to manage the flow of traffic, adding that they need to be cleared immediately to restore traffic flow.

“In case of traffic flow being affected, alternative routes should be arranged immediately,” Lanjar added. “Citizens should face minimum difficulties; traffic flow should be ensured at all costs.”

Islamabad

In Islamabad, the party staged a protest on Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed Road, formerly known as IJP Road, to mark three years since Imran’s imprisonment.

The rally was led by PTI Islamabad Regional President Amir Mughal and Regional General Secretary Malik Amir Ali Awan. Mughal told Dawn that it had been decided that only one protest would take place in the federal capital, with Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed Road selected for “a show of power”.

Participants chanted slogans and displayed placards highlighting issues including Imran’s imprisonment, the situation in Indian-occupied Kashmir, inflation, unemployment, law and order, and other matters.

Hyderabad

Similarly, the PTI staged a rally in Hyderabad, but it remained peaceful and no arrests were made by police as witnessed elsewhere.

The rally was staged on the joint call of PTI and Tehreek Tahfuz Aayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) to mark three years of Imran’s imprisonment, starting from Liberty Chowk and culminating outside the local press club. PTI Hyderabad President Mohsin Ghumman, PTI Sindh Deputy General Secretary Arif Ghafoor Sheikh and others attended.

The rally remained peaceful, but according to Mohsin Ghumman, police did not allow the demonstrators to set up camps. Police, however, didn’t make any arrests, he confirmed.

Activists and workers gathered at Hyder Chowk before reaching the local press club, where they staged a sit-in and played party songs and a recorded clip of Imran’s past speech, amid vociferous slogans.

Addressing protesters outside the press club, PTI leaders paid tributes to party workers for their steadfastness.

Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

While imprisoned, Imran has not met his family or party leaders since his sister Uzma Khanum met him last December, despite a court order from the Islamabad High Court mandating meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

His sisters have staged regular sit-ins on Tuesdays, demanding meetings with the ex-premier and that he be treated for a severe eye condition.

His eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January and he receives government-provided treatment .

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations.

The opposition has also demanded that the former premier be shifted to Shifa International Hospital, be treated in the presence of his personal physicians and allowed to meet his family.

World.title: India panel warns Meta over Modi video removal
World.content:
An Indian parliamentary panel called on Wednesday for Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg to apologise for the temporary removal of a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

India, the world’s most populous country, is Meta’s largest market by users, with hundreds of millions of people using Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

Modi’s video, addressing students during youth-led protests on July 23, was briefly removed from Meta-owned Facebook and Instagram, but was later restored.

Meta has said it was caused by technical error.

Nishikant Dubey, who heads the parliamentary committee on communications and information technology, said the panel blamed Meta.

“Deleting the prime minister’s video was not the work of an intermediary, but that of a publisher,” Dubey said, a lawmaker in Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). “Zuckerberg will have to apologise within three days.”

Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer at Meta, said he met with India’s Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Wednesday and apologised.

“I apologised to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi’s post,” Kaplan said in a statement.

India’s parliamentary standing committees scrutinise government policies and can summon officials and company executives to answer questions.

However, they cannot themselves impose penalties, revoke legal protections or direct prosecutions.

Any action against an online platform would have to be taken by the government or the courts under existing law.

Dubey said that the committee had written to the interior and technology ministries demanding action.

“If he does not apologise, then all the safe harbour protections that have been provided to his social media platforms should end,” Dubey told reporters.

Modi posted the vertical video, speaking directly to the camera, on July 23 — during the height of protests led by the online Cockroach Janta Party movement.

The demonstrations, which began in New Delhi, were sparked by anger over exam irregularities but grew into a wider movement over jobs, youth opportunities and what critics describe as Modi’s increasingly authoritarian rule.

Modi, a keen user of X, turned to Instagram — issuing his first vertical videos to tap into the youth medium of choice.

In the video, Modi assured students that the government would implement stricter laws and harsher punishments against paper leaks.

Zuckerberg apologises to India government over Meta content and errors, local media says

Zuckerberg has apologised to the Indian government over child sexual abuse material on the company’s platforms and for operational errors, local television channels reported on Wednesday.

Zuckerberg apologised for the presence of the material, as well as deepfake content and operational lapses on Meta’s platforms, financial news publication Moneycontrol reported, citing sources.

The publication added the apology was conveyed during a meeting between Meta executives and Indian government officials on Tuesday.

Meta, whose major social media apps include Facebook and Instagram, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

World.title: PM Shehbaz directs adoption of comprehensive strategy to attract investors for Discos' privatisation
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday directed relevant authorities to adopt a “comprehensive strategy” to attract international investors for the privatisation of state-owned power distribution companies (Discos) and complete the restructuring of the Privatisation Commission within one month.

“A comprehensive and effective strategy should be adopted to ensure the participation of investors meeting international standards in the privatisation of Discos,” the PM said while presiding over a review meeting in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by his office.

But, consumers’ interests should also be prioritised in the privatisation process, he instructed.

The premier further stated that all stages of the privatisation process should be completed within the stipulated timeframes and in accordance with established rules and international best practices while ensuring profitable outcomes.

He also expressed satisfaction over “successful roadshows” in Pakistan and abroad to attract investors, noting that the shows generated interest in the privatisation programme.

Officials at the meeting told the PM that the roadshows aimed at attracting investors for the Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco), Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco) and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco) in the first phase of privatisation had been concluded, according to the PMO.

It added that the meeting was told that investor outreach activities and roadshows in Turkey, Saudi Arabia and China had produced encouraging results.

The meeting was also briefed on the progress of the first phase of Discos’ privatisation and efforts to strengthen the Privatisation Commission through institutional restructuring and the recruitment of skilled professionals.

Regarding this, the PM directed that the Privatisation Commission should strengthen its workforce by recruiting experts with qualifications meeting international standards in the fields of finance, law and information technology.

Their expertise would enhance the institution’s capacity and help attract greater investment, he remarked.

PM Shehbaz also directed relevant officials to ensure that recommendations from highly qualified professional consultants were incorporated in the privatisation process and all necessary legal arrangements and financial regulatory frameworks were completed in a timely manner.

Moreover, “consumers’ interests must remain a priority during privatisation and a comprehensive and effective grievance redress mechanism be formed for the consumers of entities being privatised”, he said.

Energy Minister Sardar Awais Ahmed Khan Leghari, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja, PM’s Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali and senior government officials attended the meeting, the PMO stated.

On May 19, the Privatisation Commission had invited expressions of interest from local and international investors for the much-delayed sale of Iesco, Gepco and Fesco.

The three are considered the most viable Discos among the 11 electricity distribution companies originally carved out of the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) in 1998.

The divestment is aimed at improving service quality through private-sector management practices. The transaction offers investors an opportunity to acquire between 51pc and 100pc shareholding, along with management control, in each of the three distribution companies.

The Privatisation Commission set July 7 for submission of expressions of interest (EoIs) for Fesco, August 24 for Gepco and Sept 7 for Iesco.

In June, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali told Dawn the first Discos in the country would be sold in 2026-27.

“We will run these three parallel transactions and hold bidding one after the other in October, November and December 2026,” he said, adding the transaction structures would have to be “corrected” before October and “we will do it”.

He said the Privatisation Commission had completed domestic soft marketing of three Discos of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad in seven major cities, with chambers of commerce and industry and business houses and would now be expanding abroad mainly to Saudi Arabia, China and Turkiye and approaching other Middle Eastern capitals — Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and so on — virtually and through transaction advisers to tap in investors and technical operators.

The uniform consumer tariff will continue for the time being, but privatisation, resulting efficiency gains, and the absorption of surplus capacity would reduce the average uniform tariff, he hoped.

He said there was robust investor interest in the power sector. However, they wanted an 18pc dollar-based return, an end to uniform consumer tariffs, permission for self-power generation by new owners, freedom for the private sector to ‘buy and sell electricity’, and the government’s exit from the sector. They also wanted 8-10 year tariff visibility, including investment plans.

Ali said the government would not allow dollar-based returns at all. “We will provide rupee-based returns of 14-15pc plus key performance indicators (KPIs) that allow profitability of up to 18-20pc while sharing efficiency gains.”

Fesco, Gepco and Iesco collectively serve more than 14 million consumers across major industrial, commercial and urban centres of Punjab, the Islamabad region, and parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

Their privatisation forms part of the government’s broader economic reform agenda aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening service delivery, attracting foreign and domestic investment, and promoting sustainable growth in Pakistan’s power sector, the Privatisation Commission has said.

Alongside these three transactions, the PM’s adviser had said that the Sukkur and Hyderabad electric companies would also be restructured and improved to complete their privatisation by August-September next year.

World.title: AJK elections: PML-N, PPP secure one seat each following delayed polls in Muzaffarabad constituencies
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: The PML-N and PPP have secured one seat each in the two constituencies of Muzaffarabad division where polling was held on Tuesday after being fully or partially deferred due to landslides and adverse weather that blocked roads and prevented the timely dispatch of polling staff and election material.

The contest was part of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), during which candidates vied for seats in Muzaffarabad division and 12 seats reserved for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir.

According to official results released by the AJK Election Commission, PML-N’s Noreen Arif bagged the LA-27 (Kutla) seat with 18,919 votes, beating first runner-up, Sardar Tabarak Ali of the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) by 298 votes. PPP’s Sardar Javed Ayoub was the second runner-up, with 18,037 votes.

Meanwhile, PPP’s Syed Bazil Ali Naqvi bagged 28,214 votes to win the LA-28 (Lachhrat) seat, where PML-N’s Chaudhry Shahzad Mahmood secured 26,866 votes to emerge as the first runner-up. The third runner-up, Syed Yasir Hussain Naqvi of All Jammu and Kashmir Conference, managed to get just 873 votes.

Along with these results, the Election Commission also notified the returned candidates for the rest of the seats that were up for grabs in the second phase of the elections.

The total number of seats won by the PML-N stands at 24 while the PPP has bagged 10.

The PML-N had secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division while the PPP had secured four. After Sunday’s and Tuesday’s elections in the second phase, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third and final phase of the elections will be held in AJK’s Poonch division on August 10, during which 11 seats will be up for grabs.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns and amid protests by the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee.

Since early June, AJK has witnessed protests by the JAAC, which has been demanding the abolition of the 12 refugee seats in the AJK legislature. The protests have also been marred by violence .

World.title: Pakistan, US hold counter-terrorism dialogue, reaffirm commitment to combating terrorist groups
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The United States and Pakistan on Tuesday held the fourth counter-terrorism dialogue in Washington, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorist groups and strengthening security cooperation at a time when regional tensions remain high.

The talks were led by US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Ambassador Gregory LoGerfo and Foreign Ministry Special Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir, a joint statement released by the US State Department said.

“The dialogue underscored shared interests in the US-Pakistan counter-terrorism partnership and the two countries’ determination to confront terrorism,” the joint statement said.

“Delegations exchanged views on the current threat environment, explored avenues to enhance collaboration, and discussed steps to strengthen border security and disrupt terrorist facilitation networks,” it added.

The statement specifically named ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K), Al Qaeda, the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its affiliates among organisations that both governments said posed threats to regional security.

“The US and Pakistan affirmed their joint resolve to confront terrorist organisations that endanger the safety of their citizens and the stability of the region,” the statement said.

“The two governments committed to ensuring their counter-terrorism collaboration to keep both of their nations safe and secure, and as part of an enduring vision of regional peace, prosperity, and stability,” it said.

Meanwhile, the Foreign Office said that the two sides held “extensive deliberations on the regional and global terrorist threat and pledged to deepen counter-terrorism collaboration both bilaterally and at multilateral fora”.

The renewed engagement marks a shift from the difficult period in US-Pakistan relations following the withdrawal of American forces from Afghanistan in 2021. Washington had expressed concerns over terrorists sanctuaries in the region, while Islamabad repeatedly highlighted the security challenges it faced from cross-border militancy and instability in Afghanistan.

In recent years, both countries have sought to focus on areas of mutual interest, including counter-terrorism, trade, investment, climate cooperation, and regional stability.

Pakistan’s strategic location and longstanding diplomatic links with neighbouring countries have also increased its importance in regional diplomacy. The country’s diplomatic role also gained renewed attention during the US-Iran conflict, as Islamabad has mediated between the two sides.

The improved engagement with the US also comes as Pakistan continues to face serious internal security challenges. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

Pakistan, US look to finalise reciprocal trade framework

While representatives from the US and Pakistan held counter-terrorism discussions in Washington, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a virtual meeting with United States Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer from Islamabad.

The meeting was held to review the progress of ongoing negotiations, which are focused on strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the US, a statement released by the finance ministry said.

The engagement took place roughly three weeks after the finance minister visited Washington, where he held talks with senior American officials on trade, tariffs, investment and economic cooperation.

During his visit, Aurangzeb held meetings with officials from the Office of the Trade Representative, the US Export-Import Bank (Exim), the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and the International Monetary Fund.

The discussions focused on a possible bilateral trade agreement covering tariffs, market access, investment opportunities and wider economic cooperation. Separate talks with the Exim Bank and the DFC explored financing for infrastructure, energy and private-sector investment projects in Pakistan.

During the meeting on Wednesday, he recalled his recent discussions in Washington and “welcomed the steady progress made by the respective negotiating teams and appreciated the constructive engagement that has characterised the dialogue over time”, the finance ministry said.

It added that both sides noted that negotiations on the proposed reciprocal trade framework had advanced significantly and reaffirmed their shared commitment to conclude the agreement at the earliest.

“The finance minister highlighted the importance of maintaining the momentum of negotiations in view of Pakistan’s economic priorities.

“He emphasised that a strengthened trade and investment partnership with the United States would contribute to Pakistan’s export-led growth strategy, support economic resilience, and create greater commercial opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the statement read.

It further said that Aurangzeb also underlined the importance of continued collaboration with the Exim Bank to facilitate bilateral trade and investment.

According to the finance ministry, Ambassador Greer acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement throughout the negotiations.

He reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to “sustaining the positive trajectory of bilateral trade discussions and expressed confidence that the remaining issues could be resolved through continued technical engagement”, the finance ministry said.

It added that Aurangzeb also emphasised the importance of maintaining close coordination and accelerating technical-level discussions to build on the progress already achieved.

“Both sides expressed satisfaction with the progress achieved and agreed to continue working closely to finalise the remaining elements of the framework and agreed to continue regular engagement with a view to concluding the reciprocal trade framework soon, further strengthening the longstanding economic partnership between Pakistan and the United States,” the ministry’s statement read.

It added that Greer also “appreciated the progress made on labour and regulatory reforms, including measures relating to forced labour compliance”.

Pakistan is among the 60 countries on which the US imposed new import tariffs last month over what Washington said was their failure to effectively prohibit imports of goods produced with forced labour.

Pakistan was placed in the lower 10 per cent tariff category, alongside countries that had either adopted forced labour import prohibitions, committed to doing so under reciprocal trade arrangements, or had partial enforcement regimes.

The finance ministry said that Pakistan’s Federal Secretary for Commerce Jawad Paul and senior team members of the USTR also joined Wednesday’s meeting.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings. EV solar charging and distributed storage policies should be developed. Renewable energy skill development and employment programs should also be launched.

In the long term, within 3–10 years, Bangladesh should aim to reach more than 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030. Offshore and onshore wind should be developed. Floating solar, river-based solar, and agrivoltaics should be implemented. A National Energy Storage Strategy should be prepared. Smart grid and power sector digitalisation should be accelerated. Local assembly and manufacturing of solar panels, inverters, mounting structures, battery packs, BMS, and EV charging equipment should be encouraged. Regional power trade should be expanded. The Renewable Purchase Obligation should be introduced. Fossil fuel subsidies should be gradually redirected to a renewable energy transition fund.

Image Visual: Anwar Sohel

The benefits can be large. Energy import costs will fall. Pressure on foreign currency reserves will decline. Industrial production costs will reduce. Export competitiveness will improve. The subsidy burden will decrease. New investment will grow. Renewable energy can create 20–25 jobs per MW through rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, solar pumps, EV charging, battery storage, smart grids, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance.

The government may worry about revenue loss from tax and duty exemptions. But this should be seen as an investment. In the short term, there may be a limited impact on revenue. In the long term, Bangladesh can save far more by reducing fuel imports, lowering subsidies, saving foreign currency, strengthening industries, and attracting new investment.

Bangladesh’s energy crisis is a major challenge but also a historic opportunity. The crisis is not only a supply problem. It is a policy framework problem. Renewable energy, especially solar power, storage, and EV integration, can be among the most practical solutions for the country.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh should adopt renewable energy. The real question is how quickly, how systematically, and how boldly the country can complete this transition.



Mohammad Ataur Rahman Sarker is a renewable energy entrepreneur and the secretary of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association.

Md. Tanvir Siraj is a renewable energy researcher.

World.title: The forgotten art of Bengali advertising
World.content:
I have never seen someone at a rustic village market, anklets jingling, shouting slogans for "Khol Company’s Ringworm Ointment." No smooth-talker has ever leaned in, fanning out thin booklets like a deck of cards, whispering rhythmically, "Here are the mysteries of Gopal Bhar, and here—the secret love letters."

I never hid colourful s of a reclining Gauhar Jaan, cigarette in hand, between the folds of shirts in my drawer. I did indeed rummage through my grandfather’s pockets to collect old tram tickets, but none of them bore that curious notice for "Ashtavakra Toothpowder." Perhaps the elders of the house witnessed a tram tearing through the heart of a half-awake city, bearing the Khadi Pratisthan’s pledge for cow protection—but there was no question of me witnessing such a sight.

An iconic early 20th-century  for Bukhsh Ellahie & Co., featuring classical maestro Gauhar Jaan holding a cigarette to promote their brand

Someone’s great-grandfather might have known which drummers came beating the kara and nakara to announce, "Tonight at seven, the Chaitanya-lila folk play commences."
